q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'taciturn'?
explain: Correct: D — taciturn means habitually silent. A ('garrulous'): means excessively talkative, not quiet. B ('talkative'): is an antonym meaning fond of talking. C ('chatty'): means friendly in talk, the opposite of reserved.

q: The pacemaker of the heart is the
explain: Correct: A — the SA node starts each heartbeat. B ('atrioventricular node'): the AV node relays the signal. C ('Purkinje fibers'): Purkinje fibers spread it. D ('bundle of His'): the bundle carries it down.

q: Skin, hair, and nails make up the
explain: Correct: B — those structures cover the body. A ('skeletal system'): skeletal is bones. C ('nervous system'): nervous signals. D ('muscular system'): muscular moves.

q: In health care, the term 'edema' means
explain: Correct: D — edema is swelling caused by excess fluid in tissues. A ('bruising'): is ecchymosis, blood under skin. B ('scarring'): is healed tissue, not fluid swelling. C ('redness'): is erythema, a color change.

q: Only ___ staff may enter the pharmacy.
explain: Correct: D — personnel is the noun meaning employees. A ('personal'): personal means private. B ('personell'): personell is a misspelling. C ('persons'): persons is the plural of person, not staff collectively.

q: If T is dominant tall and t is recessive short, Tt plants are
explain: Correct: B — the dominant allele determines the trait. A ('short'): short needs tt. C ('tall and short'): one phenotype appears. D ('medium'): no blending occurs.

q: The plane dividing the body into left and right is the
explain: Correct: A — the sagittal plane makes left-right divisions. B ('oblique plane'): oblique is a diagonal cut. C ('transverse plane'): transverse divides top-bottom. D ('frontal plane'): frontal divides front-back.

q: In health care, the term 'TID' means
explain: Correct: D — TID means three times per day. A ('daily'): is the meaning of QD. B ('four times daily'): is the meaning of QID. C ('twice daily'): is the meaning of BID.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'facilitate'?
explain: Correct: D — facilitate means to make easier. A ('hinder'): is an antonym meaning to hold back. B ('obstruct'): means to block, the opposite of assist. C ('complicate'): means to make harder, not easier.

q: Fertilization normally occurs in the
explain: Correct: B — sperm meets egg in the tube. A ('uterus'): the uterus hosts implantation. C ('ovary'): the ovary releases the egg. D ('vagina'): the vagina is the entry.

q: Choose the sentence with correct pronoun-antecedent agreement. (pronoun agreement ('each nurse'))
options: Each nurse must sign his own chart.
Each nurse must sign her or his own chart.
Each nurse must sign our own chart.
Each nurse must sign their own chart.
explain: Correct: B — each nurse is singular, and her or his covers all nurses. A ('Each nurse must sign his own chart.'): his excludes nurses who are not male. C ('Each nurse must sign our own chart.'): our does not agree with each nurse. D ('Each nurse must sign their own chart.'): their is plural while each nurse is singular.

q:
According to the passage about heat stroke, what should bystanders do first?

Passage: Heat stroke is the most serious heat-related illness, occurring when the body can no longer cool itself and core temperature climbs dangerously high. Warning signs include hot, red skin, confusion, a rapid pulse, and sometimes a lack of sweating despite the heat. It is a medical emergency: bystanders should call emergency services, move the person to a cooler place, and cool them with cold cloths or a cool bath while waiting. Unlike heat exhaustion, heat stroke can cause organ damage quickly. Prevention includes hydration, shade, rest breaks, and avoiding strenuous activity in extreme heat.
options: Wait to see if it passes
explain: Correct: A — heat stroke is a medical emergency requiring a call. B ('Give the person hot tea'): hot drinks would worsen overheating. C ('Wrap the person in blankets'): blankets trap heat. D ('Wait to see if it passes'): waiting risks organ damage.

q: Which of the following is the greatest: 0.44, 4/9, 44%, or 9/20?
explain: Correct: C — In order: 9/20 = 0.45, 4/9 = 0.444, 0.44 = 0.44, 44% = 0.44. A ('44%'): it is smaller than the correct value. B ('0.44'): it is smaller than the correct value. D ('4/9'): it is smaller than the correct value.

q:
Based on the passage about pain scales, which patient would use the Wong-Baker faces scale?

Passage: Because pain is subjective, clinicians use rating scales to measure it consistently. The numeric scale asks patients to rate pain from zero, meaning no pain, to ten, meaning the worst pain imaginable. The Wong-Baker faces scale shows cartoon faces from smiling to crying and works well for children or patients with language barriers. The FLACC scale lets clinicians score pain in patients who cannot speak by observing face, legs, activity, cry, and consolability. Regular reassessment matters because pain changes, and untreated pain slows healing and raises complication risks.
options: An adult comfortable rating pain from zero to ten
A clinician assessing an unconscious patient
A four-year-old who cannot describe pain with numbers
explain: Correct: C — the faces scale suits children and language barriers. A ('An adult comfortable rating pain from zero to ten'): that patient fits the numeric scale. B ('A clinician assessing an unconscious patient'): that fits the FLACC scale. D ('A researcher studying lab results'): lab results are unrelated.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'obscure'?
explain: Correct: B — obscure means not well known or hard to see. A ('plain'): means simple and clear, not hidden. C ('evident'): means clearly visible, the opposite of obscure. D ('obvious'): is an antonym meaning easily seen.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about wound care?

Passage: Proper wound care prevents infection and speeds healing. First, stop any bleeding with gentle pressure, then clean the wound with running water; harsh scrubbing and hydrogen peroxide can damage healing tissue. Apply a thin layer of antibiotic ointment and cover with a sterile bandage, changing it daily or when wet. Watch for infection signs: increasing redness, warmth, swelling, pus, or fever. Deep wounds, animal bites, and wounds that will not stop bleeding need professional care, as do any signs of infection.
options: Gentle cleaning, covering, and watching for infection promote healing
Bandages should stay on for a week
explain: Correct: A — the passage gives the steps of home wound care. B ('Peroxide is the best cleanser'): peroxide damages tissue. C ('Bandages should stay on for a week'): bandages are changed daily. D ('All wounds need emergency care'): only serious wounds need professionals.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about advance directives?

Passage: Advance directives are legal documents that state a person's wishes for medical care if they become unable to speak for themselves. A living will describes which treatments are wanted or refused, while a health care proxy names a trusted person to make decisions. These documents only take effect when the patient cannot decide, and they can be changed at any time while the patient remains competent. Discussing wishes with family and clinicians prevents confusion during crises. Without directives, state laws decide who speaks for the patient, which may not match the patient's preferences.
options: Written wishes and a chosen proxy guide care when patients cannot decide
Directives apply while patients are competent
explain: Correct: B — the passage explains the documents and their use. A ('Family wishes always override directives'): without them, state laws choose. C ('Directives apply while patients are competent'): they take effect when the patient cannot decide. D ('Directives cannot be changed'): they can be changed while competent.

q: What is 1/5 + 3/10? Give the answer in lowest terms.
explain: Correct: A — Use a common denominator of 50: 10/50 + 15/50 = 25/50 = 1/2. B ('1/50'): the denominator was not reduced to lowest terms. C ('4/15'): added numerators and denominators straight across. D ('25/15'): added the numerators over the wrong denominator.

q: What is 3/8 + 1/4? Give the answer in lowest terms.
explain: Correct: A — Use a common denominator of 32: 12/32 + 8/32 = 20/32 = 5/8. B ('20/12'): added the numerators over the wrong denominator. C ('5/32'): the denominator was not reduced to lowest terms. D ('4/12'): added numerators and denominators straight across.

q:
In the passage about protein, the phrase "building blocks" refers to

Passage: Protein is made of building blocks called amino acids, and the body uses them to build and repair muscle, skin, enzymes, and hormones. Because the body does not store protein the way it stores fat, a steady supply from food is needed each day. Complete proteins, which contain all essential amino acids, come from animal foods as well as soy and quinoa. Incomplete proteins from beans, grains, and nuts can be combined across the day to meet needs. Most people eating a varied diet get enough protein without supplements.
options: the smaller units that make up protein
explain: Correct: D — amino acids are the units protein is made of. A ('actual bricks used in construction'): the phrase is figurative. B ('supplement pills'): supplements are said to be unnecessary for most. C ('exercise equipment'): equipment is unrelated.

q: In the scientific method, a hypothesis is
explain: Correct: B — hypotheses can be tested by experiments. A ('a random guess'): guesses are not testable. C ('a proven fact'): facts are established by evidence. D ('the final conclusion'): conclusions come after testing.

q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly? (indirect question)
options: She asked whether the pharmacy was open late!
She asked whether the pharmacy was open late.
She asked whether the pharmacy was open late?
She asked, whether the pharmacy was open late.
explain: Correct: B — an indirect question is a statement ending with a period. A ('She asked whether the pharmacy was open late!'): an exclamation point is wrong for a neutral report. C ('She asked whether the pharmacy was open late?'): an indirect question is not punctuated as a question. D ('She asked, whether the pharmacy was open late.'): no comma belongs before whether.

q: What is 2/7 x 7/8? Give the answer in lowest terms.
explain: Correct: D — Multiply numerators and denominators: 14/56 = 1/4. A ('16/49'): cross-multiplied instead of multiplying straight across. B ('9/15'): added instead of multiplying. C ('14/15'): multiplied numerators but added denominators.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about blood donation?

Passage: Donated blood saves lives every day in surgeries, cancer treatment, and emergency care, and it cannot be manufactured. Donors must generally be healthy, meet age and weight requirements, and pass a brief health screening. The donation itself takes about ten minutes, during which roughly a pint of blood is collected; the body replaces the fluid within a day and the red cells within weeks. Donors are advised to eat iron-rich foods, drink extra fluids, and avoid heavy lifting with the donation arm afterward. Most healthy adults can donate whole blood every eight weeks.
options: Blood can be manufactured in labs
Donated blood is irreplaceable, the process is quick, and donors recover fast
explain: Correct: D — the passage covers need, process, and recovery. A ('Only doctors may donate blood'): healthy adults meeting requirements may donate. B ('Donation takes several hours'): donation takes about ten minutes. C ('Blood can be manufactured in labs'): blood cannot be manufactured.

q: Gametes are produced by
explain: Correct: C — meiosis makes haploid gametes. A ('regeneration'): regeneration regrows tissue. B ('binary fission'): fission is bacterial. D ('mitosis'): mitosis keeps diploid number.

q:
According to the passage about cholesterol, what does HDL do?

Passage: Cholesterol is a waxy substance the body needs for cells and hormones, but too much in the blood damages arteries. LDL is often called bad cholesterol because it deposits plaque in artery walls, while HDL is called good cholesterol because it carries cholesterol away for disposal. Diet affects the balance: saturated and trans fats raise LDL, while fiber, exercise, and healthy weight raise HDL. A simple blood test called a lipid panel measures both types. Many people need medication in addition to lifestyle changes to reach safe levels.
explain: Correct: B — HDL is said to carry cholesterol away. A ('Stores energy as fat'): energy storage is not mentioned. C ('Deposits plaque in arteries'): that is LDL's harmful role. D ('Builds new blood cells'): blood cells are unrelated.

q: Which of the following is a run-on sentence? (run-on sentence)
options: The shift ended the nurse went home exhausted.
When the shift ended, the nurse went home exhausted.
The shift ended, and the nurse went home exhausted.
The shift ended. The nurse went home exhausted.
explain: Correct: A — two independent clauses are joined with no punctuation. B ('When the shift ended, the nurse went home exhausted.'): the dependent clause is correctly attached. C ('The shift ended, and the nurse went home exhausted.'): the comma plus and correctly joins the clauses. D ('The shift ended. The nurse went home exhausted.'): the period correctly separates the clauses.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about MRSA?

Passage: MRSA is a type of staph bacteria resistant to many common antibiotics, making its infections harder to treat. It often appears as a painful, swollen, pus-filled skin bump that can be mistaken for a spider bite. MRSA spreads through skin-to-skin contact and shared items like towels and razors, thriving in gyms, locker rooms, and health care settings. Prevention centers on handwashing, keeping cuts covered, and not sharing personal items. Suspected MRSA should be evaluated promptly rather than squeezed, since improper handling can spread the infection.
options: Drug-resistant staph spreads by contact and needs hygiene plus prompt care
explain: Correct: B — the passage covers resistance, spread, and prevention. A ('MRSA responds to all antibiotics'): it resists many common antibiotics. C ('Squeezing the bump cures it'): squeezing can spread infection. D ('Only hospitals have MRSA'): gyms and locker rooms are also named.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about fats?

Passage: Dietary fats have a bad reputation, but the body needs them to absorb certain vitamins, cushion organs, and build cell membranes. Unsaturated fats, found in olive oil, nuts, and fish, support heart health when they replace saturated fats. Saturated fats from butter, fatty meats, and full-fat dairy raise cholesterol when eaten in excess. Trans fats, once common in processed snacks, raise bad cholesterol and lower good cholesterol, and experts advise avoiding them. Reading labels for the type and amount of fat matters more than avoiding all fat.
options: Saturated fat is the healthiest choice
Some fats help health while others harm it, so type matters
explain: Correct: D — the passage compares fat types and their effects. A ('Labels never list fat content'): labels show type and amount. B ('All fat should be avoided'): the body needs fats for vitamins and cells. C ('Saturated fat is the healthiest choice'): saturated fat raises cholesterol in excess.

q: Which of the following is the greatest: 1/4, 0.3, 22%, or 2/9?
explain: Correct: A — In order: 0.3 = 0.30, 1/4 = 0.25, 2/9 = 0.222, 22% = 0.22. B ('22%'): it is smaller than the correct value. C ('1/4'): it is smaller than the correct value. D ('2/9'): it is smaller than the correct value.

q:
According to the passage about handwashing, which areas are often missed and should be scrubbed?

Passage: Washing your hands is one of the simplest and most effective ways to prevent the spread of germs. Germs from unwashed hands can enter the body through the eyes, nose, and mouth, or transfer to food and surfaces. Health experts recommend wetting hands with clean water, applying soap, and scrubbing for at least twenty seconds, making sure to clean the backs of the hands, between the fingers, and under the nails. Hands should then be rinsed well and dried with a clean towel. When soap and water are not available, a hand sanitizer with at least sixty percent alcohol can reduce germs, though it does not remove all types of dirt or chemicals.
options: The backs of the hands, between the fingers, and under the nails
explain: Correct: C — the passage names the backs of the hands, between the fingers, and under the nails. A ('Only the palms and wrists'): the passage emphasizes more than the palms. B ('The forearms and elbows'): the forearms are not mentioned. D ('Just the fingertips'): the fingertips alone are not enough.

q: In health care, the term 'NPO' means
explain: Correct: C — NPO means the patient may take nothing by mouth. A ('twice daily'): is the meaning of BID. B ('before meals'): is the meaning of ac. D ('as needed'): is the meaning of PRN.

q: Convert 0.25 g to mg.
explain: Correct: D — 1 g = 1,000 mg, so 0.25 x 1,000 = 250 mg. A ('2500'): the decimal point was moved the wrong number of places. B ('2.5'): the conversion factor was applied incorrectly. C ('25'): the conversion factor was applied incorrectly.

q: Round 3.1416 to the nearest hundredth.
explain: Correct: A — The thousandths digit is 1, so keep the hundredths digit: 3.14. B ('3.1416'): no rounding was done at all. C ('3.1'): rounded to the wrong place value. D ('3.15'): the digit was dropped without rounding up.

q: Choose the sentence with correct subject-verb agreement. (subject-verb agreement ('everyone'))
options: Everyone on the unit washing their hands often.
Everyone on the unit washes their hands often.
Everyone on the unit wash their hands often.
Everyone on the unit washes his hands often.
explain: Correct: B — everyone is singular and takes washes; their is the accepted singular pronoun. A ('Everyone on the unit washing their hands often.'): washing is a participle, not a complete verb. C ('Everyone on the unit wash their hands often.'): the singular subject everyone needs washes. D ('Everyone on the unit washes his hands often.'): his excludes people who are not male.

q: The fingers are ___ to the wrist.
explain: Correct: A — the fingers are farther from the trunk than the wrist. B ('proximal'): proximal means closer to the trunk. C ('medial'): medial is about the midline. D ('superior'): superior means above.

q:
According to the passage about eye health, what does the retina do?

Passage: Good vision depends on healthy eyes and regular care. The eye focuses light through the cornea and lens onto the retina, which converts it into signals the brain reads as images. Common problems include nearsightedness, farsightedness, and age-related changes like cataracts, a clouding of the lens. Protective habits include wearing sunglasses against ultraviolet light, taking screen breaks, and wearing safety glasses during risky tasks. Adults should have periodic eye exams, since conditions like glaucoma can damage vision silently before symptoms appear.
options: Converts light into signals the brain reads
explain: Correct: C — the retina converts light into signals. A ('Produces tears for moisture'): tear production is not the retina's job. B ('Controls pupil size'): the iris controls the pupil. D ('Focuses light onto the lens'): the cornea and lens do the focusing.

q: A catalyst speeds a reaction by
options: lowering activation energy without being consumed
explain: Correct: B — catalysts provide an easier pathway. A ('changing the products'): products stay the same. C ('being used up'): catalysts are regenerated. D ('raising activation energy'): that would slow the reaction.

q: A shift starts at 10:20 AM and ends at 4:50 PM. How long is the shift?
explain: Correct: B — From 10:20 AM to 4:20 PM is 6 hours, plus 30 minutes = 6 hours 30 minutes. A ('7 hours 30 minutes'): an extra hour was counted. C ('6 hours 10 minutes'): the minutes were added instead of subtracted correctly. D ('5 hours 30 minutes'): an hour was missed.

q:
According to the passage about dental health, what produces the acid that erodes enamel?

Passage: Tooth decay is the most common chronic disease of childhood, yet it is largely preventable. Bacteria in the mouth feed on sugars and produce acid that erodes enamel, the hard outer tooth layer. Brushing twice daily with fluoride toothpaste, flossing once a day, and limiting sugary snacks protect teeth. Fluoride strengthens enamel and can even reverse very early decay. Regular dental checkups catch cavities while they are small, and dental sealants can shield the chewing surfaces of molars in children.
explain: Correct: B — bacteria feed on sugars and produce acid. A ('Fluoride in toothpaste'): fluoride protects rather than harms. C ('Calcium in saliva'): calcium is not the acid source. D ('Water in the mouth'): water is not the acid source.

q:
Based on the passage about medications, what should a patient with bothersome side effects do?

Passage: Taking medications as prescribed, called adherence, is essential for treatment to work. Yet many patients miss doses because of cost, side effects, complex schedules, or simply forgetting. Missing doses of antibiotics can breed resistance, while skipping blood pressure or diabetes medicine quietly raises the risk of crises. Pill organizers, phone alarms, and linking doses to daily routines like brushing teeth improve consistency. Patients struggling with a regimen should tell their clinician rather than silently stopping, since doses and drugs can often be adjusted.
options: Tell the clinician so the regimen can be adjusted
Double the dose to finish faster
Stop the drug without telling anyone
explain: Correct: A — doses and drugs can often be adjusted when patients speak up. B ('Switch to a friend's medication'): sharing medications is unsafe. C ('Double the dose to finish faster'): doubling is dangerous. D ('Stop the drug without telling anyone'): silent stopping is discouraged.

q: In health care, the term 'stat' means
explain: Correct: B — stat is the order to act at once. A ('at bedtime'): is the meaning of hs. C ('daily'): is the meaning of QD. D ('as needed'): is the meaning of PRN.

q: A shift starts at 9:15 AM and ends at 1:45 PM. How long is the shift?
explain: Correct: D — From 9:15 AM to 1:15 PM is 4 hours, plus 30 minutes = 4 hours 30 minutes. A ('3 hours 30 minutes'): an hour was missed. B ('5 hours 30 minutes'): an extra hour was counted. C ('4 hours 15 minutes'): the minutes were added instead of subtracted correctly.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'erudite'?
explain: Correct: A — erudite means having great knowledge. B ('illiterate'): means unable to read, not scholarly. C ('uneducated'): means not schooled, the opposite of learned. D ('ignorant'): is an antonym meaning lacking knowledge.

q: Positively charged particles in the atom are
explain: Correct: C — protons carry a positive charge. A ('electrons'): electrons are negative. B ('photons'): photons are light particles. D ('neutrons'): neutrons are neutral.

q: Blood is classified as what tissue type?
explain: Correct: A — blood is a fluid connective tissue. B ('Nervous'): nerves signal. C ('Muscle'): muscle contracts. D ('Epithelial'): epithelium covers surfaces.

q: What number does the Roman numeral XLIX represent?
explain: Correct: B — 40 + 9 = 49, so XLIX = 49. A ('IL'): uses the wrong additive combination. C ('XILIX'): reverses part of the numeral. D ('XXXXIX'): misreads the subtractive pair.

q: Glands such as the thyroid and adrenals make up the
explain: Correct: D — those glands secrete hormones. A ('nervous system'): nervous uses electrical signals. B ('digestive system'): digestive processes food. C ('lymphatic system'): lymphatic handles immunity.

q: In health care, the term 'etiology' means
explain: Correct: D — etiology is the study or statement of a disease's cause. A ('symptom'): is the patient's complaint, not the cause. B ('outcome'): is the result, not the cause. C ('treatment'): is the intervention, not the cause.

q: The normal adult breathing rate is
explain: Correct: D — 12-20 is the normal adult range. A ('4 to 8 breaths per minute'): that is dangerously slow. B ('40 to 60 breaths per minute'): that is dangerously fast. C ('60 to 100 breaths per minute'): that is the pulse range.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about exercise?

Passage: Regular physical activity strengthens the heart, improves circulation, and helps control blood pressure and blood sugar. Aerobic exercise, such as brisk walking or swimming, trains the heart and lungs, while strength training builds the muscles that support joints and bones. Experts generally recommend at least 150 minutes of moderate activity each week, which can be broken into short sessions. Even small increases help: taking the stairs, walking during phone calls, or stretching in the morning all count. Before starting a new routine, people with health conditions should check with a clinician.
options: Walking is the only useful exercise
Exercise is unsafe for anyone with a condition
Regular activity benefits the heart, muscles, and overall health
explain: Correct: D — the passage describes types of exercise and their benefits. A ('Walking is the only useful exercise'): many activities count, including stairs and stretching. B ('Exercise is unsafe for anyone with a condition'): people with conditions should check with a clinician first. C ('Only intense workouts improve health'): moderate activity is recommended.

q: In the sentence "Neither the doctor nor the nurses were available," the verb "were" agrees with
explain: Correct: C — with neither/nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, nurses. A ('doctor'): doctor is the farther subject. B ('neither'): neither is not the subject the verb agrees with. D ('nor'): nor is a conjunction, not a subject.

q: Oxygen in Earth's early atmosphere mainly came from
explain: Correct: D — cyanobacteria oxygenated the atmosphere. A ('volcanic eruptions'): volcanoes released other gases. B ('rock weathering'): weathering does not make oxygen. C ('animal respiration'): animals consume oxygen.

q: Which sentence contains a double negative? (double negative)
options: The patient doesn't need any help walking.
The patient needs no help walking.
The patient doesn't need no help walking.
explain: Correct: D — doesn't and no create a double negative. A ('The patient doesn't need any help walking.'): any correctly pairs with doesn't. B ('The patient needs no help walking.'): needs no is a single negative. C ('The patient needs help walking.'): there is no negative at all.

q:
According to the passage about mammograms, why does early detection matter?

Passage: A mammogram is an X-ray image of the breast used to find breast cancer early, often before symptoms appear. During the exam, the breast is briefly compressed between two plates, which can cause discomfort but lasts only moments. Most guidelines suggest that women at average risk begin regular mammograms in their forties and continue as advised by their clinician. Early detection matters because smaller, earlier-stage cancers are easier to treat. A callback for extra images is common and usually turns out to be nothing serious.
options: It replaces the need for doctors
Smaller, earlier-stage cancers are easier to treat
explain: Correct: B — early-stage cancers are described as easier to treat. A ('It replaces the need for doctors'): clinician guidance is still advised. C ('It prevents all breast cancer'): mammograms detect rather than prevent. D ('It makes treatment unnecessary'): treatment is still needed, just easier.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'comply'?
explain: Correct: B — comply means to act according to a rule or request. A ('ignore'): means to pay no attention, not to follow. C ('refuse'): means to decline, the opposite of obey. D ('defy'): is an antonym meaning to resist openly.

q: In the sentence "Wow, the swelling has decreased!", the word "wow" is a(n)
explain: Correct: D — wow expresses sudden emotion, so it is an interjection. A ('adverb'): an adverb modifies a verb or adjective. B ('conjunction'): a conjunction joins words or clauses. C ('preposition'): a preposition shows a relationship.

q: The center of an atom is called the
explain: Correct: A — the nucleus holds protons and neutrons. B ('electron cloud'): electrons occupy the cloud. C ('shell'): shells hold electrons. D ('orbital'): orbitals are electron regions.

q:
According to the passage about caffeine, how does it increase alertness?

Passage: Caffeine is a stimulant found in coffee, tea, energy drinks, and chocolate. It blocks the brain's sleepiness signals, which is why a morning cup can sharpen alertness. Moderate intake is considered safe for most adults, but too much can cause jitteriness, a racing heart, and insomnia. Because caffeine lingers in the body for hours, afternoon or evening use can steal sleep, and regular heavy use can lead to dependence with headache and fatigue when skipped. People who are pregnant, anxious, or sensitive to stimulants should be especially cautious.
options: It adds extra oxygen to the blood
It blocks the brain's sleepiness signals
explain: Correct: B — caffeine is said to block sleepiness signals. A ('It adds extra oxygen to the blood'): oxygen is not mentioned. C ('It builds new brain cells'): brain cells are not mentioned. D ('It slows the heart rate'): a racing heart is a side effect, not the mechanism.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'reluctant'?
explain: Correct: A — reluctant means not wanting to do something. B ('ready'): means prepared, not hesitant. C ('eager'): is an antonym meaning keen to act. D ('willing'): means agreeable, the opposite of unwilling.

q: Antibodies are produced by
explain: Correct: A — B cells make antibodies. B ('T lymphocytes'): T cells attack directly. C ('platelets'): platelets clot. D ('red blood cells'): red cells carry oxygen.

q: In a chemical equation, the substances on the left are the
explain: Correct: D — reactants are consumed in the reaction. A ('inhibitors'): inhibitors slow reactions. B ('catalysts'): catalysts are written above arrows. C ('products'): products are on the right.

q:
According to the passage about antibiotics, what causes bacteria to become resistant?

Passage: Antibiotics are medicines that fight bacterial infections, such as strep throat and urinary tract infections. They do not work against viruses, so they cannot cure colds, flu, or most sore throats. Taking antibiotics when they are not needed, or stopping them early, helps bacteria evolve resistance, making future infections harder to treat. Patients should take the full prescribed course exactly as directed and never share leftover antibiotics with others. When used correctly, antibiotics remain one of medicine's most powerful tools.
options: Taking antibiotics when unneeded or stopping them early
explain: Correct: D — misuse is said to help bacteria evolve resistance. A ('Taking vitamins with antibiotics'): vitamins are not mentioned as a cause. B ('Resting while taking antibiotics'): rest is not mentioned as a cause. C ('Drinking water with each dose'): water is not mentioned as a cause.

q: Choose the sentence with consistent verb tense. (verb tense (past))
options: The nurse washed her hands and will enter the room.
The nurse washes her hands and entered the room.
The nurse washed her hands and entered the room.
The nurse washed her hands and enters the room.
explain: Correct: C — both verbs are past tense. A ('The nurse washed her hands and will enter the room.'): will enter shifts to future tense. B ('The nurse washes her hands and entered the room.'): washes shifts to present tense. D ('The nurse washed her hands and enters the room.'): enters shifts to present tense.

q: What is the median of 3, 7, 5, 9, 1?
explain: Correct: C — Sorted: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9; the middle value = 5. A ('3'): used the wrong measure of center. B ('1'): did not order the values first. D ('7'): an arithmetic slip changed the result.

q: What is the basic unit of life?
explain: Correct: B — the cell is the smallest unit that can live independently. A ('Molecule'): molecules are not alive. C ('Atom'): atoms are smaller but not alive. D ('Organ'): organs are made of many cells.

q: Elements in the same group on the periodic table have
explain: Correct: C — groups share valence electron counts. A ('the same number of shells'): periods share shell counts. B ('the same atomic mass'): masses increase down a group. D ('identical densities'): densities vary.

q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly? (compound sentence with 'so')
options: The EKG showed a normal rhythm, so the patient was discharged.
The EKG showed a normal rhythm so the patient was discharged.
The EKG showed a normal rhythm, the patient was discharged.
The EKG showed a normal rhythm; so the patient was discharged.
explain: Correct: A — a comma plus so correctly joins the two clauses. B ('The EKG showed a normal rhythm so the patient was discharged.'): needs a comma before so joining two clauses. C ('The EKG showed a normal rhythm, the patient was discharged.'): is a comma splice. D ('The EKG showed a normal rhythm; so the patient was discharged.'): so should not follow a semicolon here.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about choking?

Passage: Choking happens when food or an object blocks the airway, and a person who cannot cough, speak, or breathe needs immediate help. The rescuer should stand behind the person, wrap arms around the waist, and deliver quick upward thrusts above the belly button, a technique known as the Heimlich maneuver. For infants under one year, back slaps and chest thrusts are used instead. If the person becomes unresponsive, they should be lowered to the ground and CPR begun. Encouraging a person who is coughing forcefully to keep coughing is best, since the airway is only partly blocked.
options: Coughing people should never be helped
Different choking situations call for different rescue responses
The Heimlich maneuver fits every choking case
explain: Correct: B — the passage distinguishes complete blockage, infants, and partial blockage. A ('Coughing people should never be helped'): encouragement is the right help for coughing. C ('Water clears all blockages'): water is never the advised response. D ('The Heimlich maneuver fits every choking case'): infants need back slaps instead.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about stroke?

Passage: A stroke happens when blood flow to part of the brain is blocked or a brain vessel bursts, and fast treatment can prevent major disability. The FAST test helps bystanders recognize a stroke: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, and Time to call emergency services. Treatment works best within the first hours, so noting when symptoms began is critical. Risk factors include high blood pressure, smoking, diabetes, and atrial fibrillation. Calling for help immediately matters more than driving the person yourself, since paramedics can begin care on the way.
options: Driving the patient is better than calling
Recognizing stroke signs fast and calling for help prevents disability
explain: Correct: C — the passage teaches recognition and urgent response. A ('Strokes always cause permanent damage'): fast treatment can prevent major disability. B ('Driving the patient is better than calling'): paramedics begin care en route. D ('Only older adults have strokes'): no age limit is stated.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about fiber?

Passage: Fiber is the part of plant foods that the body cannot digest, and it comes in two forms. Soluble fiber dissolves in water and helps lower cholesterol and steady blood sugar; oats, beans, and apples are good sources. Insoluble fiber adds bulk to stool and helps food move through the digestive tract; whole wheat, brown rice, and vegetables provide it. Most adults need far more fiber than they eat. Increasing fiber gradually and drinking plenty of water prevents the bloating that a sudden increase can cause.

Two types of fiber aid digestion and heart health, and intake should rise gradually

B ('Fiber is fully digested for energy'): fiber is the part the body cannot digest. C ('Only supplements provide fiber'): plant foods are the sources given.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about vital signs?

Passage: Vital signs are the body's basic indicators: temperature, pulse, respiration rate, blood pressure, and often pain as a fifth sign. Temperature averages about 98.6 degrees Fahrenheit but varies through the day. A normal adult resting pulse falls between 60 and 100 beats per minute, and normal respirations between 12 and 20 breaths per minute. Blood pressure below 120 over 80 is considered normal for most adults. Trends matter more than single readings, so vital signs are recorded regularly to spot changes early.
options: Vital signs have normal ranges, and their trends reveal changes early
Single readings are all that matter
Normal ranges are identical for everyone
explain: Correct: A — the passage lists the signs, ranges, and the value of trends. B ('Single readings are all that matter'): trends matter more than single readings. C ('Normal ranges are identical for everyone'): ranges are given for most adults. D ('Pain is never assessed'): pain is often the fifth sign.

q:
Based on the passage about stress, which habit would help a stressed student?

Passage: Stress is the body's response to challenges, and in small doses it can sharpen focus. When stress becomes constant, however, it raises blood pressure, disrupts sleep, and weakens the immune system. Chronic stress is also linked to headaches, digestive problems, and anxiety. Managing stress does not require eliminating every pressure; it means building recovery into the day. Regular exercise, steady sleep, talking with trusted people, and brief relaxation practices such as slow breathing can all lower the body's stress response.
options: Taking a short walk and breathing slowly before studying
Drinking energy drinks late at night
Avoiding all friends for a month
explain: Correct: A — exercise and slow breathing are named as stress reducers. B ('Drinking energy drinks late at night'): caffeine and late nights worsen sleep. C ('Avoiding all friends for a month'): talking with trusted people is advised. D ('Skipping sleep to study longer'): steady sleep is recommended.

q:

Passage: Cholesterol is a waxy substance the body needs for cells and hormones, but too much in the blood damages arteries. LDL is often called bad cholesterol because it deposits plaque in artery walls, while HDL is called good cholesterol because it carries cholesterol away for disposal. Diet affects the balance: saturated and trans fats raise LDL, while fiber, exercise, and healthy weight raise HDL. A simple blood test called a lipid panel measures both types. Many people need medication in addition to lifestyle changes to reach safe levels.
options: Diet has no effect on cholesterol
Cholesterol types affect arteries differently, and diet, exercise, and testing manage them
explain: Correct: D — the passage explains LDL, HDL, and their management. A ('All cholesterol is harmful'): the body needs cholesterol. B ('Testing is unnecessary'): a lipid panel measures both. C ('Diet has no effect on cholesterol'): diet affects the balance.

q:
Based on the passage about antibiotics, what should a patient with a common cold do?

Passage: Antibiotics are medicines that fight bacterial infections, such as strep throat and urinary tract infections. They do not work against viruses, so they cannot cure colds, flu, or most sore throats. Taking antibiotics when they are not needed, or stopping them early, helps bacteria evolve resistance, making future infections harder to treat. Patients should take the full prescribed course exactly as directed and never share leftover antibiotics with others. When used correctly, antibiotics remain one of medicine's most powerful tools.
options: Not request antibiotics, since colds are viral
explain: Correct: A — antibiotics do not work against viruses like colds. B ('Demand antibiotics to recover faster'): antibiotics cannot cure colds. C ('Take a friend's leftover antibiotics'): leftovers should never be shared. D ('Stop all medication immediately'): the passage does not advise stopping other medication.

q:
Based on the passage about sepsis, why should a worsening infection not wait until morning?

Passage: Sepsis is the body's extreme, life-threatening response to an infection, and it can lead to tissue damage and organ failure. It begins when chemicals released to fight infection trigger widespread inflammation. Warning signs include fever or very low temperature, rapid heart rate, rapid breathing, and confusion. Every hour of delayed treatment raises the risk of death, so sepsis is a medical emergency requiring immediate care, usually with antibiotics and intravenous fluids. Anyone with an infection that is not improving should watch for these signs and seek help fast.
options: Each hour of delay raises the risk of death
explain: Correct: B — delayed treatment increases mortality. A ('Infections always improve overnight'): worsening contradicts improvement. C ('Hospitals close at night'): emergency care is always available. D ('Fever always breaks by dawn'): no such pattern is stated.

q:

Passage: Taking medications as prescribed, called adherence, is essential for treatment to work. Yet many patients miss doses because of cost, side effects, complex schedules, or simply forgetting. Missing doses of antibiotics can breed resistance, while skipping blood pressure or diabetes medicine quietly raises the risk of crises. Pill organizers, phone alarms, and linking doses to daily routines like brushing teeth improve consistency. Patients struggling with a regimen should tell their clinician rather than silently stopping, since doses and drugs can often be adjusted.

Side effects should always be endured silently
explain: Correct: A — the passage explains why adherence fails and how to improve it. B ('Missing doses has no consequences'): resistance and crises are named risks. C ('Side effects should always be endured silently'): telling the clinician is urged. D ('Complex schedules cannot be simplified'): organizers and alarms are suggested.

q:

Passage: Hospice and palliative care both focus on comfort, but they differ in timing and goals. Palliative care can begin at diagnosis alongside curative treatment, easing symptoms for anyone with serious illness. Hospice is a form of palliative care for patients near the end of life, usually when curative treatment has stopped and prognosis is measured in months. Both use teams of nurses, social workers, chaplains, and volunteers to support patients and families. Choosing hospice is not giving up; studies show it often improves quality of life in the time remaining.
options: A patient recovering from minor surgery
A patient with months to live who has stopped curative treatment
A healthy adult wanting a checkup
A newly diagnosed patient starting chemotherapy
explain: Correct: B — hospice is for end of life when curative treatment has stopped. A ('A patient recovering from minor surgery'): recovery is not end-of-life care. C ('A healthy adult wanting a checkup'): no serious illness is present. D ('A newly diagnosed patient starting chemotherapy'): that fits early palliative care.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about vaccines?

Passage: Vaccines protect people from serious diseases by training the immune system to recognize germs. A vaccine contains a weakened or inactive form of a germ, or a piece of it, which prompts the body to build defenses without causing the illness itself. When enough people in a community are vaccinated, the spread of disease slows, shielding those who cannot be vaccinated, such as newborns and people with weakened immune systems. This community protection is often called herd immunity. Common side effects, like a sore arm or mild fever, are signs the body is building protection and usually fade within a day or two.
options: Side effects prove vaccines are dangerous
Vaccines cure diseases after they start
Vaccines train the immune system and protect whole communities
Vaccines are only needed for newborn babies
explain: Correct: C — the passage covers how vaccines work and their community benefit. A ('Side effects prove vaccines are dangerous'): mild side effects are described as normal. B ('Vaccines cure diseases after they start'): vaccines prevent disease rather than cure it. D ('Vaccines are only needed for newborn babies'): the passage stresses community-wide vaccination.

q:

Standard precautions treat every patient's blood and body fluids as potentially infectious, requiring gloves, hand hygiene, and safe sharps disposal every time. Transmission-based precautions add more: contact precautions for wound infections, droplet precautions with masks for flu, and airborne precautions with special respirators for tuberculosis. Personal protective equipment must be put on before entering and removed carefully when leaving so germs are not carried out. When everyone follows these steps consistently, health care-associated infections drop sharply.
options: Layered precautions and careful protective equipment use stop infection spread
explain: Correct: D — the passage layers standard, transmission-based, and equipment steps. A ('Gloves alone prevent all infections'): hand hygiene and sharps safety are also required. B ('Only tuberculosis needs precautions'): flu and wound infections need precautions too. C ('Protective equipment is optional'): equipment must be used carefully.

explain: Correct: B — insoluble fiber is defined by adding bulk and aiding movement. A ('Lowers cholesterol'): that is soluble fiber's role. C ('Steadies blood sugar'): that is soluble fiber's role. D ('Dissolves in water'): that describes soluble fiber.

q:
Based on the passage about sprains, which injury needs prompt medical evaluation?

Passage: A sprain is a stretched or torn ligament, the tissue connecting bones at a joint, and ankles are the most common site. The RICE method guides early care: rest the joint, ice it for short periods, compress it with a bandage, and elevate it above heart level. Mild sprains improve within days, but a pop at the time of injury, inability to bear weight, or severe swelling warrants medical evaluation to rule out a fracture. Returning to activity too soon risks re-injury, so rehabilitation exercises should restore strength and balance first.
options: An ankle injury with a pop and inability to bear weight
A stiff joint the morning after exercise
A mildly sore ankle that bears weight
explain: Correct: A — a pop, inability to bear weight, or severe swelling warrants evaluation. B ('A bruise with no swelling'): no warning signs are present. C ('A stiff joint the morning after exercise'): no warning signs are present. D ('A mildly sore ankle that bears weight'): mild sprains improve within days.

q: Nerves outside the brain and spinal cord make up the
explain: Correct: A — the PNS is all other neural tissue. B ('central nervous system'): central is brain and cord. C ('cerebellum'): the cerebellum is in the brain. D ('brainstem'): the brainstem is in the brain.

explain: Correct: B — 900 / 300 = 3 tablets. A ('6 tablets'): divided the wrong way (strength / order). C ('1 1/2 tablets'): doubled the correct amount. D ('1 tablet'): halved the correct amount.

q:

Passage: The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, known as HIPAA, protects the privacy of patients' health information. It gives patients the right to see their records, request corrections, and learn who has accessed their information. Health care workers may share information only as needed for treatment, payment, or operations, and casual discussion of patients in public places violates the law. Penalties for violations can be severe, including fines and job loss. Patients who believe their privacy was violated can file a complaint with the health care provider or federal authorities.
options: Sharing lab results with the treating nurse
Giving a patient a copy of her chart
Discussing a patient's case loudly in a cafeteria
explain: Correct: D — casual public discussion violates HIPAA. A ('Sharing lab results with the treating nurse'): treatment-related sharing is allowed. B ('Giving a patient a copy of her chart'): patients have a right to their records. C ('Billing insurance for a visit'): payment operations are allowed.

explain: Correct: C — Change = 50; 50 / 200 = 0.25 = 25% increase. A ('20% increase'): divided by the new value instead of the original. B ('50% increase'): reported the dollar change as the percent. D ('25% decrease'): got the direction of the change wrong.

q:
According to the passage about organ donation, which organ can regrow after living donation?

Passage: One organ donor can save up to eight lives through heart, lung, liver, kidney, and other transplants, and tissue donation can help many more. Most organ donation happens after death, but living donors can give a kidney or part of the liver, which regenerates. Registering as a donor is usually done through a driver's license or an online registry, and sharing the decision with family is important because families are consulted. Myths persist, such as the fear that doctors will not try as hard to save a registered donor, but medical teams always prioritize saving the patient's life.
explain: Correct: C — the liver is said to regenerate after partial donation. A ('The pancreas'): the pancreas is not named. B ('The heart'): heart donation happens after death. D ('A lung'): lungs do not regenerate this way.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'vivid'?
explain: Correct: C — vivid means strikingly bright or intense. A ('faint'): means weak, not intense. B ('pale'): means light in color, the opposite of vivid. D ('dull'): is an antonym meaning lacking brightness.

explain: Correct: C — enzyme activity peaks at specific conditions. A ('Enzymes work on any substrate'): enzymes are substrate-specific. B ('Enzymes slow down all reactions'): enzymes speed reactions up. D ('Enzymes are used up in reactions'): enzymes are reusable catalysts.

explain: Correct: D — Change = 20; 20 / 80 = 0.25 = 25% decrease. A ('33% decrease'): got the direction of the change wrong. B ('25% increase'): reported the dollar change as the percent. C ('20% decrease'): divided by the new value instead of the original.

q:
Based on the passage, which person should seek care promptly?

Passage: Colds and flu are both respiratory illnesses, but they are caused by different viruses and differ in severity. Colds usually begin with a sore throat and runny nose and rarely cause serious problems. The flu tends to strike suddenly with fever, body aches, extreme tiredness, and a dry cough, and it can lead to complications like pneumonia. Because the flu spreads easily, annual vaccination, handwashing, and staying home when sick help protect others. People with trouble breathing, chest pain, or a fever that will not break should seek care promptly.
options: A cold patient with a mild runny nose
A flu patient with chest pain and trouble breathing
A healthy adult with no symptoms
A flu patient whose fever broke yesterday
explain: Correct: B — trouble breathing and chest pain are listed as warning signs. A ('A cold patient with a mild runny nose'): mild cold symptoms rarely cause serious problems. C ('A healthy adult with no symptoms'): no symptoms means no concern stated. D ('A flu patient whose fever broke yesterday'): a resolved fever is not a warning sign.

q:
In the passage about caffeine, the word "lingers" most nearly means

Passage: Caffeine is a stimulant found in coffee, tea, energy drinks, and chocolate. It blocks the brain's sleepiness signals, which is why a morning cup can sharpen alertness. Moderate intake is considered safe for most adults, but too much can cause jitteriness, a racing heart, and insomnia. Because caffeine lingers in the body for hours, afternoon or evening use can steal sleep, and regular heavy use can lead to dependence with headache and fatigue when skipped. People who are pregnant, anxious, or sensitive to stimulants should be especially cautious.
explain: Correct: B — caffeine lingers, or stays, in the body for hours. A ('tastes bitter'): taste is unrelated. C ('causes pain'): no pain meaning fits. D ('disappears instantly'): lingering is the opposite of vanishing.

q:
In the passage about burns, the word "sterile" most nearly means

Passage: Burns are classified by depth: first-degree burns affect only the outer skin, causing redness and pain; second-degree burns damage deeper layers, causing blisters; third-degree burns destroy all skin layers and may look white or charred. Minor burns should be cooled with cool running water for several minutes, then covered loosely with a sterile bandage. Ice, butter, and ointments should not be applied, as they can worsen injury or trap heat. Large burns, burns on the face or joints, and any third-degree burn need emergency care.
explain: Correct: B — a sterile bandage is germ-free. A ('brightly colored'): color is unrelated. C ('made of metal'): material is not the point. D ('very expensive'): cost is unrelated.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about depression?

Passage: Depression is more than ordinary sadness: it is a medical condition involving persistent low mood, loss of interest, and changes in sleep, appetite, and energy lasting at least two weeks. It can affect anyone and is not a sign of weakness or a choice. Effective treatments include talk therapy, medication, or a combination, and most people improve with care. If someone expresses thoughts of harming themselves, taking it seriously and connecting them with help immediately can save a life. Supporting a depressed person means listening without judgment and encouraging professional care.
options: Depression is a treatable medical condition requiring serious, compassionate response
explain: Correct: D — the passage defines depression and its treatment. A ('Depression always resolves alone'): most people improve with care. B ('Depression is a personal weakness'): it is not a sign of weakness. C ('Only medication treats depression'): therapy is also effective.

q: What is -4 + (-6)?
explain: Correct: D — adding two negatives gives a negative = -10. A ('2'): the sign of the answer is wrong. B ('-2'): the signs were combined incorrectly. C ('10'): the magnitudes were combined incorrectly.

q:
According to the passage about hospice, when can palliative care begin?

Passage: Hospice and palliative care both focus on comfort, but they differ in timing and goals. Palliative care can begin at diagnosis alongside curative treatment, easing symptoms for anyone with serious illness. Hospice is a form of palliative care for patients near the end of life, usually when curative treatment has stopped and prognosis is measured in months. Both use teams of nurses, social workers, chaplains, and volunteers to support patients and families. Choosing hospice is not giving up; studies show it often improves quality of life in the time remaining.
explain: Correct: A — palliative care can begin at diagnosis. B ('After all treatment stops'): hospice follows stopped curative treatment. C ('Only for cancer patients'): any serious illness qualifies. D ('Only in the final days'): that describes hospice timing.

q: Where does photosynthesis occur in plant cells?
explain: Correct: C — chloroplasts contain chlorophyll for photosynthesis. A ('Mitochondria'): mitochondria do respiration. B ('Vacuole'): vacuoles store materials. D ('Nucleus'): the nucleus stores DNA.

q:

Passage: A heart attack occurs when blood flow to part of the heart muscle is blocked, often by a clot in a narrowed artery. The classic warning signs are chest pressure or pain, pain spreading to the arm, neck, or jaw, shortness of breath, and cold sweats, though women and older adults may feel subtler symptoms like unusual fatigue or nausea. Chewing aspirin while waiting for help may be advised by emergency dispatchers, since it helps prevent clots from growing. Calling emergency services immediately is critical because heart muscle begins to die within minutes.
explain: Correct: B — subtler symptoms are less obvious than classic ones. A ('faster'): speed is unrelated. C ('more painful'): subtle means faint, not intense. D ('louder'): volume is unrelated.

q: Which organelle contains the cell's genetic material?

q:
According to the passage about diabetes, what happens in type 1 diabetes?

Passage: Diabetes is a condition in which blood sugar, or glucose, stays too high. Normally the pancreas releases insulin, a hormone that helps cells absorb glucose for energy. In type 1 diabetes, the body makes little or no insulin and daily insulin is required. In type 2 diabetes, the more common form, cells resist insulin's effects, and it is often managed with lifestyle changes and medication. Warning signs include frequent urination, constant thirst, and unexplained fatigue. Managing diabetes means keeping blood sugar in a target range through diet, activity, medication, and regular monitoring.
options: The body makes little or no insulin
The pancreas makes too much insulin
explain: Correct: B — type 1 is defined as little or no insulin production. A ('Cells resist insulin's effects'): that describes type 2 diabetes. C ('Blood sugar drops too low'): diabetes involves high, not low, blood sugar. D ('The pancreas makes too much insulin'): the problem is too little insulin, not too much.

q: In health care, the term 'tachycardia' means
explain: Correct: D — tachycardia is an abnormally rapid heartbeat. A ('irregular rhythm'): is arrhythmia, not specifically fast. B ('slow heart rate'): is bradycardia. C ('high blood pressure'): is hypertension, a pressure not a rate.

explain: Correct: C — ominous means giving the impression something bad will happen. A ('hopeful'): means optimistic, not menacing. B ('reassuring'): is an antonym meaning comforting. D ('promising'): means favorable, the opposite of threatening.

q: How many valence electrons does oxygen have?
explain: Correct: C — oxygen is in group 16, with 6 outer electrons. A ('4'): 4 is incorrect for oxygen. B ('8'): 8 is the total electron count. D ('2'): 2 is the first-shell count.

explain: Correct: A — -osis means an abnormal condition, as in osteoporosis. B ('removal'): is the meaning of -ectomy. C ('pain'): is the meaning of -algia. D ('inflammation'): is the meaning of -itis.

explain: Correct: B — DNA contains deoxyribose. A ('Ribose'): ribose is in RNA. C ('Sucrose'): sucrose is table sugar. D ('Glucose'): glucose is an energy sugar.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'candid'?
explain: Correct: A — candid means truthful and straightforward. B ('vague'): means unclear, not direct. C ('deceptive'): means misleading, the opposite of candid. D ('reserved'): means holding back, not openly honest.

explain: Correct: A — 4 x 3 + 1 = 13, so 13/3 = 13/3. B ('12/3'): the remainder was computed incorrectly. C ('13/4'): the whole number and fraction were mixed up. D ('11/3'): multiplied instead of dividing, or vice versa.

explain: Correct: B — 400 / 8 = 50 mg per tablet; 50 x 5 = 250 mg. A ('50'): used the wrong per-tablet amount. C ('640'): set up the proportion backwards. D ('2000'): multiplied instead of dividing first.

explain: Correct: C — osteons are the Haversian systems of bone. A ('nephron'): nephrons are kidney units. B ('lobule'): lobules are liver units. D ('sarcomere'): sarcomeres are muscle units.

explain: Correct: C — amino acids polymerize into proteins. A ('Glucose - lipids'): glucose builds carbohydrates. B ('Fatty acids - DNA'): fatty acids build lipids. D ('Nucleotides - starch'): nucleotides build nucleic acids.

q:
Based on the passage about UTIs, which symptom pattern needs prompt care?

Passage: A urinary tract infection, or UTI, occurs when bacteria enter the urethra and multiply in the bladder. Symptoms include a strong urge to urinate, burning during urination, cloudy urine, and pelvic discomfort. Women get UTIs far more often than men because of shorter urethras. Drinking water, urinating after intercourse, and wiping front to back reduce risk. Most simple UTIs are treated with a short course of antibiotics, but symptoms plus fever or back pain may signal a kidney infection needing prompt care.
options: Mild urgency that resolves in a day
Burning urination plus fever and back pain
Cloudy urine with no other symptoms
explain: Correct: C — fever and back pain may signal kidney infection. A ('A single episode years ago'): a past episode is not current. B ('Mild urgency that resolves in a day'): resolving symptoms are less urgent. D ('Cloudy urine with no other symptoms'): one mild symptom is less concerning.

q:
In the passage about MRSA, the word "resistant" most nearly means

Passage: MRSA is a type of staph bacteria resistant to many common antibiotics, making its infections harder to treat. It often appears as a painful, swollen, pus-filled skin bump that can be mistaken for a spider bite. MRSA spreads through skin-to-skin contact and shared items like towels and razors, thriving in gyms, locker rooms, and health care settings. Prevention centers on handwashing, keeping cuts covered, and not sharing personal items. Suspected MRSA should be evaluated promptly rather than squeezed, since improper handling can spread the infection.
explain: Correct: B — resistant bacteria survive common antibiotics. A ('weakened by'): resistance means survival, not weakening. C ('unaware of'): awareness is unrelated. D ('attracted to'): attraction is unrelated.

q: In health care, the term 'malignant' means
explain: Correct: B — malignant describes cancer that invades and spreads. A ('contained'): is the opposite of spreading. C ('healing'): is recovery, not the term's meaning. D ('harmless'): is the meaning of benign.

explain: Correct: C — two reactants combine into one product. A ('single replacement'): replacement swaps elements. B ('decomposition'): decomposition breaks one into many. D ('double replacement'): double replacement swaps partners.

q: What is 0.25 as a fraction in lowest terms?

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about eye health?

Passage: Good vision depends on healthy eyes and regular care. The eye focuses light through the cornea and lens onto the retina, which converts it into signals the brain reads as images. Common problems include nearsightedness, farsightedness, and age-related changes like cataracts, a clouding of the lens. Protective habits include wearing sunglasses against ultraviolet light, taking screen breaks, and wearing safety glasses during risky tasks. Adults should have periodic eye exams, since conditions like glaucoma can damage vision silently before symptoms appear.
options: Eyes convert light to images, and protection plus exams preserve vision
explain: Correct: C — the passage explains vision and its protection. A ('Glasses cure all eye problems'): exams catch silent conditions. B ('Only children need eye exams'): adults need periodic exams. D ('Sunglasses are purely cosmetic'): UV protection is a stated benefit.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about quitting smoking?

Passage: Quitting smoking is the single most important step a smoker can take for health. Within weeks of quitting, circulation improves and coughing eases; within a year, the risk of heart disease drops sharply. Many smokers worry about weight gain or cravings, but these effects are temporary and far less harmful than continued smoking. Effective strategies include setting a quit date, removing tobacco from the home, and using support such as counseling or nicotine replacement. Most successful quitters try several times before succeeding, so a relapse should be treated as a lesson rather than a failure.
options: Only medication can help smokers quit
Quitting is easy on the first try
Quitting brings fast benefits, and setbacks are part of the process
explain: Correct: D — the passage lists benefits, strategies, and the normality of relapse. A ('Only medication can help smokers quit'): counseling is also listed as support. B ('Weight gain makes quitting unwise'): weight gain is far less harmful than smoking. C ('Quitting is easy on the first try'): most quitters try several times.

q: In medical terminology, '-stasis' means
explain: Correct: C — -stasis means standing still, as in hemostasis. A ('growth'): is the meaning of -plasia. B ('movement'): is the opposite, -kinesia. D ('flow'): is the opposite of the suffix's meaning.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about hydration?

Passage: Water makes up about sixty percent of the adult human body and plays a role in nearly every bodily function. It carries nutrients to cells, flushes out waste, cushions joints, and helps regulate body temperature through sweating. Even mild dehydration can cause headaches, fatigue, and difficulty concentrating. While daily needs vary with activity level and climate, a common guideline is to drink enough fluid that urine stays pale yellow. Fruits, vegetables, and soups also contribute to fluid intake, so hydration does not come from drinks alone.
options: Only plain water counts toward hydration
Adults need exactly eight glasses daily
Water supports nearly every body function, so steady intake matters
explain: Correct: D — the passage lists water's roles and how to stay hydrated. A ('Only plain water counts toward hydration'): fruits and soups also contribute fluid. B ('Dehydration has no noticeable symptoms'): headaches and fatigue are named symptoms. C ('Adults need exactly eight glasses daily'): needs vary and no exact number is given.

q: The first line of immune defense includes
explain: Correct: A — barriers block pathogens first. B ('vaccines'): vaccines train immunity in advance. C ('T cells'): T cells are cellular immunity. D ('antibodies'): antibodies are a later response.

q:

Passage: Colorectal cancer often grows slowly from small growths called polyps, and screening can find and remove polyps before they turn cancerous. A colonoscopy, in which a flexible camera examines the colon, is the most thorough screening test and is usually repeated every ten years when results are normal. Stool-based tests are a less invasive option done more often. Most guidelines advise starting regular screening at age forty-five for people at average risk. Because early colorectal cancer rarely causes symptoms, waiting for warning signs can mean missing the best window for prevention.
options: Screening is dangerous before that age
Cancer grows slowly and silently, so screening must start before symptoms
explain: Correct: D — early cancer rarely causes symptoms, so routine screening starts at the guideline age. A ('Polyps only appear at forty-five'): polyps grow over time rather than appearing suddenly. B ('Screening is dangerous before that age'): no danger claim is made. C ('Symptoms always appear by forty-five'): the passage says symptoms rarely appear early.

q:

Smoking is the leading cause, though long-term exposure to dust and fumes can also contribute. Hallmark symptoms are a chronic cough, excess mucus, wheezing, and shortness of breath that worsens with activity. While lung damage cannot be reversed, quitting smoking, pulmonary rehabilitation, and prescribed inhalers slow the decline and improve daily life. Vaccination against flu and pneumonia is especially important because infections hit COPD patients harder.
explain: Correct: D — hallmark symptoms are the characteristic ones. A ('painful'): pain is not the meaning. B ('invisible'): symptoms are noticeable. C ('rare'): hallmark means defining, not rare.
