The nurses notes were thorough and legible.
The nurse's notes were thorough and legible.
explain: Correct: D — nurse's is the singular possessive; one nurse wrote the notes. A ('The nurse's notes' were thorough and legible.'): notes' adds a second possessive error. B ('The nurses' notes were thorough and legible.'): nurses' is plural possessive, but one nurse is meant. C ('The nurses notes were thorough and legible.'): the possessive needs an apostrophe.

q: Convert 750 mg to g.
explain: Correct: D — 1,000 mg = 1 g, so 750 / 1,000 = 0.75 g. A ('0.075'): the decimal point was moved the wrong number of places. B ('75'): the conversion factor was applied incorrectly. C ('7.5'): the conversion factor was applied incorrectly.

q: In the sentence "The results, which arrived late, changed the plan," the word "which" is a(n)
explain: Correct: B — which introduces the relative clause describing the results. A ('interrogative pronoun'): an interrogative pronoun asks a question. C ('demonstrative pronoun'): a demonstrative pronoun points, like that. D ('indefinite pronoun'): an indefinite pronoun is vague, like some.

q: A price changes from $40 to $50. What is the percent increase?
explain: Correct: C — Change = 10; 10 / 40 = 0.25 = 25% increase. A ('20% increase'): divided by the new value instead of the original. B ('25% decrease'): got the direction of the change wrong. D ('10% increase'): reported the dollar change as the percent.

q:
According to the passage about the thyroid, what characterizes hyperthyroidism?

Passage: The thyroid is a butterfly-shaped gland in the neck that produces hormones regulating metabolism, the pace of the body's processes. In hypothyroidism, the gland underproduces, causing fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, and slowed thinking. In hyperthyroidism, it overproduces, causing weight loss, rapid heartbeat, anxiety, and heat intolerance. Both conditions are diagnosed with blood tests and usually managed with daily medication. Because thyroid hormones affect nearly every organ, untreated disorders can strain the heart and other systems over time.
options: Only neck swelling with no symptoms
Overproduction causing weight loss and rapid heartbeat
explain: Correct: C — hyperthyroidism is overproduction with those symptoms. A ('Only neck swelling with no symptoms'): systemic symptoms are listed. B ('No hormone production at all'): some production continues. D ('Underproduction causing weight gain'): that describes hypothyroidism.

q: The umbilical cord connects the fetus to the
explain: Correct: B — the placenta exchanges nutrients and waste. A ('bladder'): the bladder is unrelated. C ('uterus wall directly'): the cord attaches via the placenta. D ('ovary'): ovaries are uninvolved.

q: The smallest functional unit of the nervous system is the
explain: Correct: D — neurons carry nerve impulses. A ('alveolus'): alveoli exchange gases. B ('sarcomere'): sarcomeres contract muscle. C ('nephron'): nephrons filter blood.

q: What is 2/3 - 1/6? Give the answer in lowest terms.
explain: Correct: C — Use a common denominator of 18: 12/18 - 3/18 = 9/18 = 1/2. A ('9/21'): used the wrong common denominator. B ('1/-3'): subtracted numerators and denominators straight across. D ('9/9'): subtracted the numerators over the wrong denominator.

q: What is 7/10 as a percent?
explain: Correct: B — 7/10 = 0.7, and 0.7 x 100 = 70%. A ('700%'): multiplied by 1000 instead of 100. C ('0.07%'): divided by 10 instead of multiplying by 100. D ('7%'): multiplied by 10 instead of 100.

q: Where does the Krebs cycle occur?
explain: Correct: A — the Krebs cycle runs in the mitochondrial matrix. B ('Cytoplasm'): glycolysis is cytoplasmic. C ('Ribosome'): ribosomes build proteins. D ('Thylakoid'): thylakoids host light reactions.

q: In medical terminology, '-phobia' means
explain: Correct: A — -phobia means irrational fear, as in claustrophobia. B ('discharge'): is the meaning of -rrhea. C ('love'): is the meaning of -philia. D ('pain'): is the meaning of -algia.

q: In the sentence "The bandage was too tight," the word "tight" is a(n)
explain: Correct: D — tight describes the noun bandage, so it is an adjective. A ('adverb'): an adverb modifies a verb or adjective. B ('verb'): a verb shows action. C ('noun'): a noun names a person, place, or thing.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about tuberculosis?

Passage: Tuberculosis, or TB, is a bacterial infection that most often attacks the lungs and spreads through the air when an infected person coughs. Many infected people have latent TB, meaning the bacteria are inactive and they feel no symptoms and cannot spread it. Active TB causes a persistent cough, sometimes with blood, along with fever, night sweats, and weight loss. Treatment requires taking several antibiotics for many months, and stopping early can create drug-resistant TB. Testing is recommended for people with prolonged exposure or symptoms.
options: Treatment takes only a few days
TB spreads through air, may stay latent, and needs months of treatment
explain: Correct: C — the passage covers transmission, latency, and treatment. A ('Treatment takes only a few days'): months of antibiotics are required. B ('Latent TB is highly contagious'): latent cases cannot spread it. D ('TB spreads through contaminated water'): it spreads when an infected person coughs.

q: Which of the following is the greatest: 3/4, 0.72, 70%, or 7/10?
explain: Correct: D — In order: 3/4 = 0.75, 0.72 = 0.72, 70% = 0.70, 7/10 = 0.70. A ('7/10'): it is smaller than the correct value. B ('0.72'): it is smaller than the correct value. C ('70%'): it is smaller than the correct value.

q: In health care, the term 'hypertrophy' means
explain: Correct: C — hypertrophy is growth in the size of cells or tissue. A ('death'): is necrosis, not growth. B ('shrinkage'): is atrophy, the opposite. D ('inflammation'): is -itis, not enlargement.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about dehydration?

Passage: Dehydration occurs when the body loses more fluid than it takes in, through sweating, vomiting, diarrhea, or simply not drinking enough. Early signs include thirst, dry mouth, and dark yellow urine; as it worsens, dizziness, rapid heartbeat, and confusion can appear. Children and older adults are at higher risk because their bodies regulate fluid less effectively. Mild dehydration often improves with steady sipping of water or oral rehydration solutions, but severe signs like fainting or no urination need emergency care. Preventing dehydration means drinking before feeling thirsty during heat or illness.
options: Fluid loss causes worsening symptoms, and severe cases need emergency care
explain: Correct: D — the passage traces causes, signs, and treatment. A ('Thirst is the only symptom'): many signs beyond thirst are listed. B ('Dehydration is never serious'): fainting needs emergency care. C ('Only water causes dehydration'): fluid loss, not water, is the cause.

q: What is 3/4 + 5/8? Give the answer in lowest terms.
explain: Correct: B — Use a common denominator of 32: 24/32 + 20/32 = 44/32 = 11/8. A ('8/12'): added numerators and denominators straight across. C ('11/32'): the denominator was not reduced to lowest terms. D ('44/12'): added the numerators over the wrong denominator.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'feasible'?
explain: Correct: B — feasible means able to be done. A ('impossible'): is an antonym meaning not able to be done. C ('impractical'): means not practical, the opposite of possible. D ('unworkable'): means unable to work, not doable.

q:
In the passage about back pain, the word "culprits" most nearly means

Passage: Back pain is one of the most common reasons people miss work, and most cases stem from muscle strain rather than serious disease. Poor posture, prolonged sitting, and lifting with the back instead of the legs are frequent culprits. Prevention focuses on ergonomics: sitting with support for the lower back, taking movement breaks, and strengthening core muscles that stabilize the spine. Most episodes improve within weeks with gentle activity, since prolonged bed rest can actually slow recovery. Warning signs needing prompt care include numbness in the legs, loss of bladder control, or pain after significant trauma.
explain: Correct: C — poor posture and sitting are the culprits, or causes. A ('victims'): sufferers are not the meaning. B ('doctors'): doctors treat rather than cause. D ('criminals'): no crime is involved.

q: The change from gas to liquid is called
explain: Correct: C — condensation is gas to liquid. A ('evaporation'): evaporation is liquid to gas. B ('melting'): melting is solid to liquid. D ('deposition'): deposition is gas to solid.

q:
According to the passage about vital signs, what is the normal adult resting pulse range?

Passage: Vital signs are the body's basic indicators: temperature, pulse, respiration rate, blood pressure, and often pain as a fifth sign. Temperature averages about 98.6 degrees Fahrenheit but varies through the day. A normal adult resting pulse falls between 60 and 100 beats per minute, and normal respirations between 12 and 20 breaths per minute. Blood pressure below 120 over 80 is considered normal for most adults. Trends matter more than single readings, so vital signs are recorded regularly to spot changes early.
explain: Correct: C — 60 to 100 is the stated normal range. A ('20 to 40 beats per minute'): that range is far too low. B ('100 to 120 beats per minute'): that range is too high. D ('40 to 60 beats per minute'): that range is too low.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'verbose'?
explain: Correct: C — verbose means using more words than needed. A ('terse'): means sparing with words, the opposite of wordy. B ('concise'): is an antonym meaning brief. D ('brief'): means short, not long-winded.

q: The nurse needs ___ to the supply room.
explain: Correct: D — access is the noun meaning entry or the right to enter. A ('assess'): assess means to evaluate. B ('axes'): axes are tools or the plural of axis. C ('excess'): excess means a surplus.

q: What is 5 - 1.25?
explain: Correct: D — Line up the decimal points: 5.00 - 1.25 = 3.75. A ('37.5'): an arithmetic slip changed a digit. B ('4.75'): the decimal point is in the wrong place. C ('3.25'): the decimal point is in the wrong place.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about calcium?

Passage: Calcium is the most abundant mineral in the body, and nearly all of it is stored in bones and teeth. Bones constantly rebuild themselves, breaking down old tissue and forming new tissue, a process that requires a steady supply of calcium and vitamin D. When the diet lacks calcium, the body pulls the mineral from bones, gradually weakening them. Good sources include dairy products, fortified plant milks, leafy greens, and canned fish with bones. Weight-bearing exercise, such as walking or dancing, also helps bones stay dense and strong.
options: Calcium and vitamin D, plus exercise, keep bones strong
explain: Correct: A — the passage covers calcium's role, sources, and bone-building habits. B ('Only dairy provides calcium'): plant milks and greens are also sources. C ('Bones never change after childhood'): bones constantly rebuild. D ('Calcium is unimportant for adults'): adults need steady calcium to protect bones.

q: Which of the following is the greatest: 7/10, 0.68, 71%, or 2/3?
explain: Correct: B — In order: 71% = 0.71, 7/10 = 0.70, 0.68 = 0.68, 2/3 = 0.667. A ('0.68'): it is smaller than the correct value. C ('7/10'): it is smaller than the correct value. D ('2/3'): it is smaller than the correct value.

q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly? (period ending a statement (x-ray))
explain: Correct: B — a plain statement ends with a period. A ('The x-ray showed no fractures!'): an exclamation point overstates a routine finding. C ('The x-ray showed no fractures?'): a statement is not a question. D ('The X-ray showed no fractures.'): x-ray is correctly lowercased as a common noun.

q: A shift starts at 8:45 AM and ends at 5:15 PM. How long is the shift?
explain: Correct: A — From 8:45 AM to 4:45 PM is 8 hours, plus 30 minutes = 8 hours 30 minutes. B ('8 hours 15 minutes'): an extra hour was counted. C ('9 hours 30 minutes'): the minutes were added instead of subtracted correctly. D ('7 hours 30 minutes'): an hour was missed.

q:
Based on the passage about fats, which snack choice fits the advice?

Passage: Dietary fats have a bad reputation, but the body needs them to absorb certain vitamins, cushion organs, and build cell membranes. Unsaturated fats, found in olive oil, nuts, and fish, support heart health when they replace saturated fats. Saturated fats from butter, fatty meats, and full-fat dairy raise cholesterol when eaten in excess. Trans fats, once common in processed snacks, raise bad cholesterol and lower good cholesterol, and experts advise avoiding them. Reading labels for the type and amount of fat matters more than avoiding all fat.
options: A handful of almonds instead of a processed pastry
Butter spread thick on white bread
Skipping all food containing any fat
A snack cake made with trans fats
explain: Correct: A — nuts supply unsaturated fats while pastries may contain trans fats. B ('Butter spread thick on white bread'): butter is high in saturated fat. C ('Skipping all food containing any fat'): the body needs some fat. D ('A snack cake made with trans fats'): trans fats should be avoided.

q: Choose the sentence with correct subject-verb agreement. (subject-verb agreement ('neither/nor'))
options: Neither the nurse nor the aides was late.
Neither the nurse nor the aides be late.
Neither the nurse nor the aides were late.
Neither the nurse nor the aides are late.
explain: Correct: C — the verb agrees with the nearer subject aides, so were is correct. A ('Neither the nurse nor the aides was late.'): was agrees with nurse, not the nearer subject. B ('Neither the nurse nor the aides be late.'): be is not a correct past-tense form. D ('Neither the nurse nor the aides are late.'): are is present tense, but the sentence is past.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about dental health?

Passage: Tooth decay is the most common chronic disease of childhood, yet it is largely preventable. Bacteria in the mouth feed on sugars and produce acid that erodes enamel, the hard outer tooth layer. Brushing twice daily with fluoride toothpaste, flossing once a day, and limiting sugary snacks protect teeth. Fluoride strengthens enamel and can even reverse very early decay. Regular dental checkups catch cavities while they are small, and dental sealants can shield the chewing surfaces of molars in children.
options: Decay is common but preventable through hygiene, fluoride, and checkups
Adults do not need dental care
explain: Correct: A — the passage explains decay's cause and its prevention. B ('Brushing alone guarantees no cavities'): flossing and diet also matter. C ('Adults do not need dental care'): checkups are recommended for all. D ('Decay is rare in children'): it is called the most common childhood chronic disease.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'vacant'?
explain: Correct: B — vacant means containing nothing. A ('crowded'): means packed, not empty. C ('full'): means filled, the opposite of empty. D ('occupied'): is an antonym meaning in use.

q: What happens to an enzyme at very high temperature?
options: It works twice as fast forever
explain: Correct: A — heat breaks the protein's shape. B ('It becomes more specific'): specificity is lost, not gained. C ('It works twice as fast forever'): extreme heat destroys function. D ('It turns into a carbohydrate'): it does not change macromolecule type.

q: Lactose is broken down by the enzyme
explain: Correct: D — lactase digests lactose. A ('amylase'): amylase digests starch. B ('pepsin'): pepsin digests protein. C ('lipase'): lipase digests lipids.

q: Which sentence has correct adjective order? (adjective order)
options: She carried small a black bag.
She carried a small black bag.
She carried a black small bag.
She carried a bag small black.
explain: Correct: B — size comes before color in standard adjective order. A ('She carried small a black bag.'): articles come before adjectives. C ('She carried a black small bag.'): color should follow size. D ('She carried a bag small black.'): adjectives come before the noun.

q: In health care, the term 'hypertension' means
explain: Correct: C — hypertension is persistently elevated arterial pressure. A ('low blood pressure'): is hypotension. B ('fast pulse'): is tachycardia, a rate not a pressure. D ('chest pain'): is a symptom, not the pressure term.

q: ADP becomes ATP mainly in the
explain: Correct: A — mitochondria phosphorylate ADP. B ('ribosome'): ribosomes build proteins. C ('lysosome'): lysosomes digest. D ('nucleus'): the nucleus stores DNA.

q: Round 9.49 to the nearest tenth.
explain: Correct: B — The hundredths digit is 9, so round the tenths digit up: 9.5. A ('9.4'): the digit was dropped without rounding up. C ('9.49'): no rounding was done at all. D ('9'): rounded to the wrong place value.

q:
According to the passage about nutrition labels, what does the serving size determine?

Passage: Nutrition labels help shoppers compare foods and make informed choices. The serving size listed at the top is the key to the whole label: all the calories and nutrients shown are for one serving, not the entire package. Percent Daily Values tell how much a nutrient in a serving contributes to a day's diet, with five percent or less considered low and twenty percent or more considered high. Shoppers watching sodium, added sugars, or saturated fat can use these percentages to compare products quickly. Ingredients are listed from most to least by weight, so the first few ingredients make up most of the food.
options: How many servings are in the package
What all the calorie and nutrient numbers on the label refer to
The expiration date of the food
explain: Correct: B — all numbers on the label are for one serving. A ('How many servings are in the package'): the label shows servings per container separately. C ('The expiration date of the food'): expiration dates are not on nutrition labels. D ('The price per serving'): prices are not on nutrition labels.

q:
In the passage about allergies, the word "auto-injector" refers to

Passage: Allergies occur when the immune system overreacts to a normally harmless substance, such as pollen, pet dander, or certain foods. The body releases histamine, which causes sneezing, itchy eyes, and a runny nose. Most allergies are managed with avoidance and antihistamines, but some people develop anaphylaxis, a severe reaction that can close the airway and drop blood pressure. Anaphylaxis is a medical emergency treated with an epinephrine auto-injector, followed by a call to emergency services. Anyone prescribed an auto-injector should carry it at all times.
options: a device that delivers epinephrine quickly
explain: Correct: C — it is used to treat anaphylaxis with epinephrine. A ('a breathing machine'): it injects medicine rather than assisting breathing. B ('a type of vaccine'): it treats reactions rather than preventing disease. D ('a blood pressure cuff'): it delivers drugs rather than measuring pressure.

q: Sweat glands are located in the
explain: Correct: A — glands sit in the dermal layer. B ('hypodermis'): hypodermis is mostly fat. C ('epidermis'): the epidermis has no glands. D ('stratum corneum'): that is the top of the epidermis.

q: An atom with 6 protons and 6 neutrons has a mass number of
explain: Correct: D — 6 + 6 = 12. A ('18'): 18 would add electrons wrongly. B ('0'): mass is never zero. C ('6'): 6 is the atomic number.

q: Which compound is held together by covalent bonds?
explain: Correct: B — carbon shares electrons with hydrogen. A ('Calcium fluoride'): CaF2 is ionic. C ('Sodium chloride'): NaCl is ionic. D ('Magnesium oxide'): MgO is ionic.

q: The collarbone is called the
explain: Correct: B — the clavicle is the collarbone. A ('scapula'): the scapula is the shoulder blade. C ('sternum'): the sternum is the breastbone. D ('humerus'): the humerus is the arm bone.

q:
The author's purpose in the passage about antibiotics is to

Passage: Antibiotics are medicines that fight bacterial infections, such as strep throat and urinary tract infections. They do not work against viruses, so they cannot cure colds, flu, or most sore throats. Taking antibiotics when they are not needed, or stopping them early, helps bacteria evolve resistance, making future infections harder to treat. Patients should take the full prescribed course exactly as directed and never share leftover antibiotics with others. When used correctly, antibiotics remain one of medicine's most powerful tools.
options: teach correct use and prevent resistance
explain: Correct: C — the passage instructs proper use and warns about resistance. A ('describe how antibiotics are manufactured'): manufacturing is never discussed. B ('argue that antibiotics are useless'): antibiotics are called powerful tools. D ('advertise a new antibiotic drug'): no drug is advertised.

q:
Based on the passage about hypothermia, why should wet clothing be removed?

Passage: Hypothermia sets in when the body loses heat faster than it can produce it, dropping core temperature below 95 degrees Fahrenheit. Early signs are shivering and clumsiness; as it worsens, shivering may stop, speech slurs, and thinking grows confused. Wet clothing, wind, and cold water accelerate heat loss, which is why hikers and boaters are at risk. To help, move the person to shelter, remove wet clothing, and warm them gradually with blankets and warm drinks, never alcohol. Severe hypothermia needs emergency care, since the heart becomes dangerously irritable.
options: Wet clothing keeps the body warm
explain: Correct: B — wet clothing is listed as accelerating heat loss. A ('Dry clothing causes shivering'): shivering is an early sign regardless. C ('Wet clothing keeps the body warm'): wetness increases heat loss. D ('Wet clothing prevents confusion'): confusion comes from cold, not clothing.

q: The order is for 1500 mg. The tablets contain 500 mg each. How many tablets should be given?
explain: Correct: D — 1500 / 500 = 3 tablets. A ('6 tablets'): divided the wrong way (strength / order). B ('2 tablets'): halved the correct amount. C ('1 1/2 tablets'): doubled the correct amount.

q: What is 3/5 x 5/6? Give the answer in lowest terms.
explain: Correct: A — Multiply numerators and denominators: 15/30 = 1/2. B ('15/11'): multiplied numerators but added denominators. C ('18/25'): cross-multiplied instead of multiplying straight across. D ('8/11'): added instead of multiplying.

q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly? (capitalizing titles)
options: Dr Patel ordered the blood test.
Dr. patel ordered the blood test.
Dr. Patel ordered the blood test.
dr. Patel ordered the blood test.
explain: Correct: C — titles are abbreviated with a period and names capitalized. A ('Dr Patel ordered the blood test.'): Dr. needs its period. B ('Dr. patel ordered the blood test.'): Patel is a proper noun needing a capital. D ('dr. Patel ordered the blood test.'): dr. is a title needing a capital.

q: A covalent bond forms when electrons are
explain: Correct: D — sharing holds covalent molecules together. A ('converted to neutrons'): particles do not convert. B ('lost to the environment'): electrons are conserved. C ('transferred completely'): transfer makes ionic bonds.

q: Simplify the ratio 21:28 to lowest terms.
explain: Correct: B — Divide both terms by 7 = 3:4. A ('21:4'): did not simplify at all. C ('4:3'): inverted the ratio. D ('7:7'): only partly simplified.

q: Which gas is released by photosynthesis?
explain: Correct: D — oxygen is the byproduct of photosynthesis. A ('Nitrogen'): nitrogen is not exchanged. B ('Hydrogen'): hydrogen is not released. C ('Carbon dioxide'): CO2 is taken in.

q: The magician created a clever optical ___.
explain: Correct: A — illusion is a false visual impression. B ('allusion'): allusion is an indirect reference. C ('elusion'): elusion is evasion, unrelated. D ('lucid'): lucid means clear, an adjective.

q: Which group includes bacteria?
explain: Correct: D — bacteria are prokaryotic cells. A ('Plants'): plants are eukaryotes. B ('Fungi'): fungi are eukaryotes. C ('Protists'): protists are eukaryotes.

q: A car travels 180 miles in 3 hours. What is the average speed in miles per hour?
explain: Correct: C — 180 / 3 = 60 mph. A ('90 mph'): divided the wrong way. B ('540 mph'): multiplied instead of dividing. D ('6 mph'): dropped a zero.

q: The atomic number of an element equals its number of
explain: Correct: B — atomic number is defined by proton count. A ('neutrons'): neutrons vary in isotopes. C ('isotopes'): isotopes are variants. D ('electrons plus neutrons'): that sum is the mass number.

q: Saturated fats differ from unsaturated fats because saturated fats
options: are always liquid at room temperature
have no double bonds between carbons
explain: Correct: D — saturation means single bonds only. A ('are always liquid at room temperature'): saturated fats are solid at room temperature. B ('cannot be digested'): both are digestible. C ('have many double bonds'): that describes unsaturated fats.

q: A price changes from $90 to $72. What is the percent decrease?
explain: Correct: B — Change = 18; 18 / 90 = 0.20 = 20% decrease. A ('20% increase'): reported the dollar change as the percent. C ('25% decrease'): divided by the new value instead of the original. D ('18% decrease'): got the direction of the change wrong.

q: How many chromosomes are in a human gamete?
explain: Correct: B — gametes carry half the chromosomes. A ('22'): 22 omits a sex chromosome. C ('46'): 46 is the body cell number. D ('12'): 12 is incorrect.

q: Which of the following is a sentence fragment? (fragment (relative clause))
options: The medication that the doctor prescribed yesterday.
The doctor prescribed the medication, and the nurse gave it.
The doctor prescribed the medication yesterday.
explain: Correct: A — that turns it into a dependent clause with no main clause. B ('The doctor prescribed the medication, and the nurse gave it.'): it has two complete clauses joined correctly. C ('The doctor prescribed the medication yesterday.'): it has a subject and verb forming a complete thought. D ('The medication worked quickly.'): it has a subject and verb forming a complete thought.

q: The hormone that stimulates milk production is
explain: Correct: B — prolactin drives milk synthesis. A ('insulin'): insulin handles glucose. C ('oxytocin'): oxytocin ejects milk. D ('cortisol'): cortisol handles stress.

q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly? (imperative sentence)
options: Turn off your phone before entering the unit.
Turn off, your phone before entering the unit.
Turn off your phone, before entering the unit.
Turn off your phone; before entering the unit.
explain: Correct: A — an imperative sentence needs no internal comma. B ('Turn off, your phone before entering the unit.'): the comma wrongly separates the verb from its object. C ('Turn off your phone, before entering the unit.'): the comma wrongly splits the command. D ('Turn off your phone; before entering the unit.'): a semicolon cannot join a phrase to a clause.

q: What happens during cytokinesis?
options: The cytoplasm divides into two cells
explain: Correct: A — cytokinesis splits the cytoplasm. B ('The nuclear envelope breaks down'): that is prophase. C ('DNA replicates'): that is S phase. D ('Chromosomes condense'): that is prophase.

q: The order is for 0.5 g. The supply is 250 mg per 5 mL. How many mL should be given?
explain: Correct: D — First convert 0.5 g to 500 mg; 500 / 250 = 2 doses of 5 mL = 10 mL. A ('20 mL'): doubled the correct volume. B ('5 mL'): divided the wrong way (concentration / order). C ('2.5 mL'): used the concentration as the volume directly.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'redundant'?
explain: Correct: A — redundant means unnecessarily repeated. B ('concise'): is an antonym meaning brief. C ('essential'): means necessary, the opposite of superfluous. D ('brief'): means short, not wordy.

q: A child inherits one allele from each parent because
explain: Correct: C — fertilization combines two haploid gametes. A ('mitosis doubles the alleles'): mitosis keeps chromosome number. B ('mutations create alleles'): mutations are rare changes. D ('proteins split evenly'): proteins are not inherited this way.

q: The master gland of the endocrine system is the
explain: Correct: A — the pituitary controls other glands. B ('adrenal'): adrenals are controlled by the pituitary. C ('pancreas'): the pancreas is partly controlled too. D ('thyroid'): thyroid is controlled by the pituitary.

q: Convert 2:45 PM to military time.
explain: Correct: D — Add 12 to a PM hour: 2 + 12 = 14, so 2:45 PM = 1445. A ('0245'): 12 was never added for the PM hour. B ('0215'): the minutes were misread. C ('1345'): added 11 instead of 12.

q: How many chromosomes do human body cells have?
explain: Correct: C — humans have 23 pairs, or 46 chromosomes. A ('44'): 44 omits the sex chromosomes. B ('48'): 48 is incorrect for humans. D ('23'): 23 is the gamete number.

q: What is 1/50 as a decimal?
explain: Correct: D — Divide 1 by 50: 1 / 50 = 0.02. A ('0.002'): the decimal point is one place too far left. B ('0.2'): the decimal point is one place too far right. C ('0.150'): the fraction's digits were written as a decimal without dividing.

q:
Based on the passage about hearing, which worker most needs hearing protection?

Passage: Hearing loss often develops gradually, and many people do not notice it until others point it out. Loud noise is a leading preventable cause: sounds above 85 decibels, about the level of city traffic, can damage hearing with prolonged exposure, and a single gunshot or explosion can cause instant harm. Earplugs or earmuffs at concerts, around machinery, and while using power tools protect the delicate inner-ear structures. Warning signs include ringing in the ears, needing higher TV volume, and difficulty following conversations. Early evaluation matters because treatment works best before loss progresses.
options: A construction worker using a jackhammer daily
A gardener planting flowers by hand
explain: Correct: A — prolonged loud machinery exposure risks damage. B ('A librarian shelving books'): libraries are quiet. C ('An office worker typing quietly'): typing is far below 85 decibels. D ('A gardener planting flowers by hand'): hand gardening is quiet.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'contaminate'?
explain: Correct: D — contaminate means to make impure by contact. A ('sterilize'): means to kill germs, the opposite of contaminate. B ('purify'): is an antonym meaning to make pure. C ('cleanse'): means to clean, the opposite of pollute.

q: What is the mode of 5, 5, 8, 8, 5, 3?
explain: Correct: A — 5 appears three times, more than any other value = 5. B ('5 and 8'): miscounted the values. C ('8'): used the wrong measure of center. D ('3'): an arithmetic slip changed the result.

q: Blood clotting is mainly the job of
explain: Correct: B — platelets form the initial plug. A ('white blood cells'): white cells fight infection. C ('plasma proteins only'): proteins help but platelets lead. D ('red blood cells'): red cells carry oxygen.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'serene'?
explain: Correct: B — serene means peaceful and untroubled. A ('noisy'): means loud, the opposite of serene. C ('turbulent'): is an antonym meaning chaotic. D ('anxious'): means worried, the opposite of calm.

q: Which sugar is found in RNA?
explain: Correct: D — RNA contains ribose. A ('Fructose'): fructose is a fruit sugar. B ('Deoxyribose'): deoxyribose is in DNA. C ('Galactose'): galactose is a milk sugar.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about pneumonia?

Passage: Pneumonia is an infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid or pus. Symptoms include cough with phlegm, fever, chills, and difficulty breathing. It can be caused by bacteria, viruses, or fungi, and treatment depends on the cause: bacterial pneumonia needs antibiotics, while viral cases need rest and supportive care. Older adults, young children, and people with weakened immunity face the highest risk of complications. Vaccines against pneumococcal bacteria and the flu lower the risk of the most common forms.
options: Pneumonia inflames the lungs, varies by cause, and is preventable by vaccine
explain: Correct: D — the passage covers definition, causes, treatment, and prevention. A ('Vaccines are useless against pneumonia'): vaccines lower the risk. B ('Pneumonia only affects the elderly'): children are also at risk. C ('All pneumonia needs antibiotics'): viral cases need supportive care.

q: What is 0.6 as a fraction in lowest terms?
explain: Correct: C — 0.6 = 6/10 = 3/5. A ('2/3'): that fraction does not equal the decimal. B ('3/4'): that fraction does not equal the decimal. D ('1/2'): that fraction does not equal the decimal.

q:
Based on the passage about hypoglycemia, why is juice preferred over a candy bar with nuts?

Passage: Hypoglycemia means blood sugar has dropped too low, most often in people with diabetes who take insulin or certain medications. Early symptoms include shakiness, sweating, hunger, and a fast heartbeat; if untreated, confusion, slurred speech, and loss of consciousness can follow. The standard treatment is the 15-15 rule: consume 15 grams of fast-acting carbohydrate, such as glucose tablets or juice, wait 15 minutes, and recheck. Skipping meals, extra exercise, and too much medication are common triggers. Anyone who faints or cannot swallow needs emergency help rather than food or drink.
options: Juice has no sugar at all
Fast-acting carbohydrate raises blood sugar quickly
explain: Correct: B — fast-acting carbohydrate is the specified treatment. A ('Juice has no sugar at all'): juice contains fast sugar. C ('Candy bars are always forbidden'): no absolute ban is stated. D ('Nuts cure hypoglycemia faster'): fat in nuts slows absorption.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about arthritis?

Passage: Arthritis means joint inflammation, but the term covers more than a hundred conditions. Osteoarthritis, the most common type, results from cartilage wearing down over time, causing stiffness that often eases with movement. Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the joints, often affecting both sides of the body symmetrically. Management for both includes staying active, maintaining a healthy weight to reduce joint load, and using medications as prescribed. Joint replacement surgery is an option only when conservative measures no longer control pain and function.
options: Arthritis has many forms, with activity and weight control central to management
All arthritis is the same disease
explain: Correct: C — the passage contrasts two types and their management. A ('Surgery is the first treatment'): surgery is a last option. B ('Rest is the only therapy'): staying active is recommended. D ('All arthritis is the same disease'): over a hundred conditions are covered.

q:
According to the passage about Alzheimer's, what are early signs?

Passage: Alzheimer's disease is the most common cause of dementia, gradually destroying memory and thinking skills. Early signs include forgetting recently learned information, difficulty planning, and confusion about time or place. As it progresses, patients may struggle with familiar tasks, withdraw socially, and experience personality changes. There is no cure, but medications and structured routines can temporarily ease symptoms, and caregiver support is essential. Regular physical activity, social engagement, and managing blood pressure may lower risk, though none guarantees prevention.
options: Forgetting recent information and confusion about time or place
explain: Correct: D — early signs listed are forgetting recent information and confusion. A ('Rapid improvement in memory'): memory worsens rather than improves. B ('A high fever with rash'): fever and rash are unrelated. C ('Sudden paralysis on one side'): paralysis suggests stroke, not Alzheimer's.

q:
In the passage about generics, the word "counterparts" most nearly means

Passage: Generic drugs contain the same active ingredient, strength, and dosage form as their brand-name counterparts, and regulators require them to work the same way in the body. Because generic makers do not repeat the costly original research, generics typically cost far less. Inactive ingredients like fillers and dyes may differ, which occasionally matters for people with specific sensitivities. Pharmacists may substitute a generic automatically where laws allow, though prescribers can require the brand. Asking whether a generic exists is one of the simplest ways to lower prescription costs.
explain: Correct: C — brand-name counterparts are the matching brand versions. A ('opponents in a debate'): no debate is involved. B ('copies of a key'): versions, not keys, are meant. D ('parts of a machine'): drugs are not machine parts.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'stagnant'?
explain: Correct: D — stagnant means showing no movement or progress. A ('flowing'): is an antonym meaning moving steadily. B ('lively'): means full of life, not still. C ('dynamic'): means changing energetically, the opposite of stagnant.

q: Urine leaves the body through the
explain: Correct: A — the urethra is the exit tube. B ('bladder'): the bladder stores urine. C ('ureter'): ureters go to the bladder. D ('nephron'): nephrons filter blood.

q:
According to the passage about sleep, what happens in the body during sleep?

Passage: Sleep is essential for both the body and the mind. During sleep, the brain organizes memories, the body repairs tissue, and hormones that control growth and appetite are regulated. Adults generally need seven to nine hours of sleep each night, yet many fall short because of late-night screen use, caffeine, and irregular schedules. Poor sleep is linked to trouble concentrating, weakened immunity, and a higher risk of accidents. Simple habits can help: keeping a consistent bedtime, making the bedroom dark and cool, and avoiding screens for at least thirty minutes before bed.
options: Tissue is repaired and hormones are regulated
explain: Correct: A — the passage states the body repairs tissue and regulates hormones. B ('Digestion stops completely'): digestion is not said to stop. C ('The heart stops beating'): the heart keeps beating during sleep. D ('Muscles grow weaker'): repair strengthens rather than weakens.

q:
In the passage about diabetes, the word "absorb" most nearly means

Passage: Diabetes is a condition in which blood sugar, or glucose, stays too high. Normally the pancreas releases insulin, a hormone that helps cells absorb glucose for energy. In type 1 diabetes, the body makes little or no insulin and daily insulin is required. In type 2 diabetes, the more common form, cells resist insulin's effects, and it is often managed with lifestyle changes and medication. Warning signs include frequent urination, constant thirst, and unexplained fatigue. Managing diabetes means keeping blood sugar in a target range through diet, activity, medication, and regular monitoring.
explain: Correct: C — cells absorb, or take in, glucose for energy. A ('destroy'): absorption is uptake, not destruction. B ('ignore'): cells use glucose rather than ignoring it. D ('give off'): cells take glucose in rather than release it.

q: Which pH is the most acidic?
explain: Correct: C — lower pH means stronger acid. A ('7'): 7 is neutral. B ('5'): 5 is weakly acidic. D ('9'): 9 is basic.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'enhance'?
explain: Correct: B — enhance means to raise quality or value. A ('weaken'): means to make weaker, the opposite of improve. C ('reduce'): means to make smaller, not better. D ('diminish'): is an antonym meaning to lessen.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'impartial'?
explain: Correct: D — impartial means treating all sides equally. A ('biased'): is an antonym meaning prejudiced. B ('unfair'): describes an unjust result, not neutrality. C ('partial'): means favoring one side, the opposite of impartial.

q: The plane dividing the body into front and back is the
explain: Correct: D — the frontal plane makes anterior-posterior divisions. A ('median plane'): median is a type of sagittal. B ('sagittal plane'): sagittal divides left-right. C ('transverse plane'): transverse divides top-bottom.

q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly? (appositive commas)
options: My sister a nurse works at County General.
My sister, a nurse works at County General.
My sister a nurse, works at County General.
My sister, a nurse, works at County General.
explain: Correct: D — the appositive a nurse needs commas on both sides. A ('My sister a nurse works at County General.'): an appositive needs surrounding commas. B ('My sister, a nurse works at County General.'): the second comma is missing. C ('My sister a nurse, works at County General.'): the first comma is missing.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about severe bleeding?

Passage: Severe bleeding is a life-threatening emergency that requires fast action. The first step is to press firmly on the wound with a clean cloth or bandage and maintain steady pressure without lifting it to check. If blood soaks through, add more layers on top rather than removing the first one. For bleeding on an arm or leg that will not stop, a tourniquet placed a few inches above the wound can save a life, and the time it was applied should be noted. Emergency services should be called immediately in every case of severe bleeding.
options: Bleeding always stops on its own
Fast, steady pressure and calling for help save lives
Water is the best first treatment
explain: Correct: C — the passage gives the steps for controlling severe bleeding. A ('Bleeding always stops on its own'): severe bleeding is called life-threatening. B ('Minor cuts need tourniquets'): tourniquets are for bleeding that will not stop. D ('Water is the best first treatment'): pressure, not water, is the first step.

q:
According to the passage about seizures, what is the correct order of first-aid steps?

Passage: A seizure is a sudden burst of electrical activity in the brain, and most end on their own within a couple of minutes. During a convulsive seizure, the priority is safety: ease the person to the floor, cushion the head, loosen tight clothing, and move sharp objects away. Nothing should be placed in the mouth, and the person should not be restrained. Afterward, roll them onto their side if unconscious and stay until fully alert. Emergency care is needed for seizures lasting over five minutes, repeated seizures, or breathing difficulty afterward.
options: Give water during the seizure, then walk the person around
Restrain the limbs, then insert a mouth guard
Ease to floor, cushion head, clear objects, roll to side after
explain: Correct: D — the passage orders easing down, cushioning, clearing, then recovery position. A ('Leave immediately, then return later'): staying until alert is required. B ('Give water during the seizure, then walk the person around'): water and walking are not advised. C ('Restrain the limbs, then insert a mouth guard'): restraint and mouth objects are prohibited.

q: Microvilli increase a cell's
explain: Correct: A — folds of microvilli expand absorptive surface. B ('genetic material'): DNA amount is unchanged. C ('waste storage'): vacuoles store waste. D ('energy output'): mitochondria make energy.

q: Which is a physical change?
explain: Correct: A — boiling changes state only. B ('Baking bread'): baking forms new substances. C ('Rusting iron'): rusting forms new compounds. D ('Digesting food'): digestion breaks molecules.

q:
According to the passage about sugar, why are sugary drinks especially concerning?

Passage: Added sugars sweeten foods and drinks but provide calories with almost no nutrients. Sodas, candy, pastries, and many breakfast cereals are leading sources, and sugary drinks are especially concerning because they deliver a large sugar load without making people feel full. High intake is linked to weight gain, tooth decay, and a greater risk of type 2 diabetes. Naturally occurring sugars in fruit and milk come packaged with fiber, vitamins, and minerals, making them a better choice. Checking labels for added sugars helps shoppers spot hidden sources like sauces and flavored yogurts.
options: They replace the need for water
They deliver much sugar without making people feel full
They contain no sugar at all
explain: Correct: C — the passage states they do not create fullness. A ('They are always sugar-free'): sugary drinks are not sugar-free. B ('They replace the need for water'): water needs are separate. D ('They contain no sugar at all'): they are described as a leading source.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'withdraw'?
explain: Correct: C — withdraw means to take back or pull away. A ('deposit'): means to put in, the opposite of remove. B ('insert'): means to place inside, not to take away. D ('advance'): is an antonym meaning to move forward.

q: The left side of the heart pumps blood to the
explain: Correct: A — the left heart drives systemic circulation. B ('lungs'): the right heart serves the lungs. C ('heart itself only'): coronary arteries are a small branch. D ('right atrium'): flow goes forward, not backward.

q: Solve for x: 2(x + 3) = 16
explain: Correct: C — x + 3 = 8, so x = 5, so x = 5. A ('2'): made a sign error. B ('8'): undid the operations in the wrong order. D ('13'): only undid one of the two operations.

q: The fluid cushioning the brain and spinal cord is

When enough people in a community are vaccinated, the spread of disease slows, shielding those who cannot be vaccinated, such as newborns and people with weakened immune systems. This community protection is often called herd immunity. Common side effects, like a sore arm or mild fever, are signs the body is building protection and usually fade within a day or two.
options: immunity that only farm animals develop
a vaccine made from animal products
protection that lasts only one year
community-wide protection that shields vulnerable people
explain: Correct: D — herd immunity is described as community protection for those who cannot be vaccinated. A ('immunity that only farm animals develop'): the term is about human communities. B ('a vaccine made from animal products'): the passage never mentions animal products. C ('protection that lasts only one year'): no time limit is stated.

q: Convert 3:00 PM to military time.
explain: Correct: C — Add 12 to a PM hour: 3 + 12 = 15, so 3:00 PM = 1500. A ('1400'): added 11 instead of 12. B ('0330'): the minutes were misread. D ('0300'): 12 was never added for the PM hour.

q: The nurse walked ___ the waiting room to reach the elevator.
explain: Correct: C — past is the preposition meaning beyond. A ('pass'): pass is the present-tense verb. B ('passed'): passed is the past tense of the verb pass. D ('paste'): paste is a noun or verb for adhesive.

q: What is 5/6 - 1/3? Give the answer in lowest terms.
explain: Correct: A — Use a common denominator of 18: 15/18 - 6/18 = 9/18 = 1/2. B ('4/3'): subtracted numerators and denominators straight across. C ('9/24'): used the wrong common denominator. D ('9/9'): subtracted the numerators over the wrong denominator.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about heat stroke?

Passage: Heat stroke is the most serious heat-related illness, occurring when the body can no longer cool itself and core temperature climbs dangerously high. Warning signs include hot, red skin, confusion, a rapid pulse, and sometimes a lack of sweating despite the heat. It is a medical emergency: bystanders should call emergency services, move the person to a cooler place, and cool them with cold cloths or a cool bath while waiting. Unlike heat exhaustion, heat stroke can cause organ damage quickly. Prevention includes hydration, shade, rest breaks, and avoiding strenuous activity in extreme heat.
options: Heat stroke is an emergency needing fast cooling and prevention through caution
Heat stroke is the mildest heat illness
explain: Correct: A — the passage defines, treats, and prevents heat stroke. B ('Heat stroke is the mildest heat illness'): it is called the most serious. C ('Sweating always prevents heat stroke'): lack of sweating can occur. D ('Only athletes get heat stroke'): no group is singled out.

q:
According to the passage about CPR, how deep should adult compressions be?

Passage: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation, or CPR, keeps blood flowing to the brain and heart when someone's heart has stopped. For adults, the rescuer pushes hard and fast in the center of the chest, about two inches deep, at a rate of 100 to 120 compressions per minute, allowing full chest recoil between pushes. Rescue breaths are no longer required for untrained bystanders; continuous compressions alone can double or triple survival chances. An automated external defibrillator, or AED, should be used as soon as one arrives. Calling emergency services first ensures advanced help is on the way.
explain: Correct: C — the passage specifies about two inches deep. A ('About four inches'): four inches would be too deep. B ('About half an inch'): half an inch would be too shallow. D ('As deep as possible'): depth is specified, not unlimited.

q: 2 tablets contain 500 mg of medication. How many mg are in 7 tablets?
explain: Correct: A — 500 / 2 = 250 mg per tablet; 250 x 7 = 1750 mg. B ('700'): set up the proportion backwards. C ('250'): used the wrong per-tablet amount. D ('3500'): multiplied instead of dividing first.

q: How is the number 68 written in Roman numerals?
explain: Correct: B — LXVIII = 68, so 68 = LXVIII. A ('LXVII'): uses a nonstandard combination. C ('LXXVIII'): adds instead of subtracting. D ('LXVIIII'): misuses the subtractive pair.

q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly? (question marks in quotations)
options: The patient asked, When will I see the doctor?
The patient asked "when will I see the doctor?"
The patient asked, "When will I see the doctor?"
The patient asked, "When will I see the doctor."
explain: Correct: C — the question mark stays inside the quotes for a quoted question. A ('The patient asked, When will I see the doctor?'): direct speech needs quotation marks. B ('The patient asked "when will I see the doctor?"'): a comma must introduce the quotation and when needs a capital. D ('The patient asked, "When will I see the doctor."'): a quoted question needs a question mark, not a period.

q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly? (commas in a series)
options: Wash your hands before eating; after coughing; and after using the restroom.
Wash your hands: before eating, after coughing, and after using the restroom.
Wash your hands before eating, after coughing, and after using the restroom.
Wash your hands before eating after coughing and after using the restroom.
explain: Correct: C — commas separate the three items in the series. A ('Wash your hands before eating; after coughing; and after using the restroom.'): semicolons are too strong for a simple series. B ('Wash your hands: before eating, after coughing, and after using the restroom.'): a colon cannot follow the verb wash here. D ('Wash your hands before eating after coughing and after using the restroom.'): items in a series need separating commas.

q: Most water absorption occurs in the
explain: Correct: B — the large intestine reclaims water. A ('pancreas'): the pancreas secretes enzymes. C ('stomach'): the stomach digests. D ('small intestine'): the small intestine absorbs nutrients.

q: What is 0.875 as a fraction in lowest terms?
explain: Correct: D — 0.875 = 875/1000 = 7/8. A ('8/9'): that fraction does not equal the decimal. B ('7/9'): that fraction does not equal the decimal. C ('6/7'): that fraction does not equal the decimal.

q: A solution with pH 7 is
explain: Correct: C — 7 is the neutral point. A ('acidic'): acidic is below 7. B ('caustic'): caustic means strongly basic. D ('basic'): basic is above 7.

q: The largest organ of the human body is the
explain: Correct: C — skin is the largest organ by area and weight. A ('heart'): the heart is much smaller. B ('lung'): lungs are smaller. D ('liver'): the liver is the largest internal organ.

q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly? (capitalizing months)
options: January is national blood donor month.
January is National Blood Donor Month
january is National Blood Donor Month.
January is National Blood Donor Month.
explain: Correct: D — the month is capitalized and the statement needs a period. A ('January is national blood donor month.'): the title of the observance is capitalized. B ('January is National Blood Donor Month'): a statement needs ending punctuation. C ('january is National Blood Donor Month.'): january is a proper noun needing a capital.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about skin cancer?

Passage: The ABCDE rule helps people spot melanomas, the most dangerous skin cancers: Asymmetry, where halves do not match; Border irregularity; Color variation; Diameter larger than a pencil eraser; and Evolving, meaning any change over time. Most skin cancers are not melanoma but basal or squamous cell types, which grow slowly and rarely spread yet still need treatment. Risk rises with sunburn history, fair skin, and tanning bed use. Any mole matching ABCDE warning signs deserves prompt professional evaluation rather than watchful waiting.
options: The ABCDE rule flags dangerous moles for prompt evaluation
explain: Correct: D — the passage teaches the warning-sign rule. A ('Moles should never be checked'): regular checking is implied by the rule. B ('Tanning beds are safe'): tanning beds raise risk. C ('All skin cancers are melanoma'): other types are also described.

q: Convert 200 cm to m.
explain: Correct: C — 100 cm = 1 m, so 200 / 100 = 2 m. A ('2000'): the decimal point was moved the wrong number of places. B ('0.2'): the conversion factor was applied incorrectly. D ('20'): the conversion factor was applied incorrectly.

q: What number does the Roman numeral IX represent?
explain: Correct: A — 9 = 9, so IX = 9. B ('IV'): reverses part of the numeral. C ('VIIII'): uses the wrong additive combination. D ('XI'): misreads the subtractive pair.

q: DNA is shaped like a
explain: Correct: B — DNA is a twisted double helix. A ('single strand'): RNA can be single-stranded. C ('triple coil'): no triple coil exists. D ('flat sheet'): proteins fold into sheets.

q:
According to the passage about choking, what should you do for a forcefully coughing person?

Passage: Choking happens when food or an object blocks the airway, and a person who cannot cough, speak, or breathe needs immediate help. The rescuer should stand behind the person, wrap arms around the waist, and deliver quick upward thrusts above the belly button, a technique known as the Heimlich maneuver. For infants under one year, back slaps and chest thrusts are used instead. If the person becomes unresponsive, they should be lowered to the ground and CPR begun. Encouraging a person who is coughing forcefully to keep coughing is best, since the airway is only partly blocked.
options: Perform the Heimlich maneuver at once
Pat them hard on the back
explain: Correct: C — forceful coughing means the airway is only partly blocked. A ('Perform the Heimlich maneuver at once'): the maneuver is for those who cannot cough. B ('Pat them hard on the back'): back slaps are for infants. D ('Give them water to drink'): water is not advised.

q: 5 tablets contain 1000 mg of medication. How many mg are in 3 tablets?
explain: Correct: C — 1000 / 5 = 200 mg per tablet; 200 x 3 = 600 mg. A ('1500'): multiplied instead of dividing first. B ('300'): set up the proportion backwards. D ('200'): used the wrong per-tablet amount.

q: A group of similar cells working together is a
explain: Correct: D — tissues are cell groups with a shared function. A ('cell'): a cell is the single unit. B ('system'): systems contain multiple organs. C ('organ'): organs contain multiple tissues.

q: What is 2/3 + 3/4? Give the answer in lowest terms.
explain: Correct: B — Use a common denominator of 12: 8/12 + 9/12 = 17/12 = 17/12. A ('18/12'): the denominator was not reduced to lowest terms. C ('5/7'): added numerators and denominators straight across. D ('17/7'): added the numerators over the wrong denominator.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'zealous'?
explain: Correct: C — zealous means showing great energy for a cause. A ('indifferent'): means unconcerned, the opposite of zealous. B ('apathetic'): is an antonym meaning showing no interest. D ('reluctant'): means unwilling, not eager.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'mundane'?
explain: Correct: A — mundane means dull and everyday. B ('exciting'): means thrilling, the opposite of ordinary. C ('remarkable'): means notable, not routine. D ('extraordinary'): is an antonym meaning exceptional.

q:
In the passage about handwashing, the word "transfer" most nearly means

Passage: Washing your hands is one of the simplest and most effective ways to prevent the spread of germs. Germs from unwashed hands can enter the body through the eyes, nose, and mouth, or transfer to food and surfaces. Health experts recommend wetting hands with clean water, applying soap, and scrubbing for at least twenty seconds, making sure to clean the backs of the hands, between the fingers, and under the nails. Hands should then be rinsed well and dried with a clean towel. When soap and water are not available, a hand sanitizer with at least sixty percent alcohol can reduce germs, though it does not remove all types of dirt or chemicals.
options: move from one place to another
explain: Correct: D — germs transfer, or move, from hands to food and surfaces. A ('disappear completely'): germs spread rather than vanish. B ('grow in number'): transfer does not mean multiply. C ('become harmless'): germs remain harmful after transfer.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'succinct'?
explain: Correct: C — succinct means briefly and clearly expressed. A ('lengthy'): is an antonym meaning long. B ('wordy'): means using too many words, the opposite of succinct. D ('rambling'): means wandering, not brief.

q: The first electron shell holds a maximum of
explain: Correct: A — the first shell fits 2 electrons. B ('1 electron'): 1 is hydrogen's count, not the max. C ('18 electrons'): 18 is for higher shells. D ('8 electrons'): outer shells hold 8.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about portions?

Passage: Portion sizes have grown dramatically over recent decades, and larger servings quietly encourage overeating. Studies show people tend to eat what is put in front of them, finishing bigger portions without feeling proportionally fuller. Simple strategies help: using smaller plates, serving food in the kitchen rather than at the table, and pausing halfway through a meal to assess fullness. Reading labels reveals that many packages contain multiple servings. Eating slowly also matters, since the brain needs about twenty minutes to register fullness.
options: Portion sizes have shrunk over time
Bigger servings drive overeating, but simple strategies restore control
explain: Correct: D — the passage explains the problem and its solutions. A ('Portion sizes have shrunk over time'): portions have grown. B ('Overeating is purely about willpower'): environmental cues are the focus, not willpower. C ('Labels never show serving counts'): labels reveal multiple servings.

q: Sugar-free ___ was served after dinner.
explain: Correct: D — dessert is the sweet food served after a meal. A ('desert'): desert is an arid region. B ('deserted'): deserted means abandoned. C ('deserts'): deserts is the plural of that region.

q: The skin is ___ to the muscles.
explain: Correct: A — the skin lies closer to the surface. B ('proximal'): proximal is about the trunk. C ('deep'): deep means farther from the surface. D ('superior'): superior means above.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about handwashing?

Passage: Washing your hands is one of the simplest and most effective ways to prevent the spread of germs. Germs from unwashed hands can enter the body through the eyes, nose, and mouth, or transfer to food and surfaces. Health experts recommend wetting hands with clean water, applying soap, and scrubbing for at least twenty seconds, making sure to clean the backs of the hands, between the fingers, and under the nails. Hands should then be rinsed well and dried with a clean towel. When soap and water are not available, a hand sanitizer with at least sixty percent alcohol can reduce germs, though it does not remove all types of dirt or chemicals.
options: Germs are only spread in hospitals
Drying hands is more important than washing them
Hand sanitizer works better than soap and water
Proper handwashing is a simple, effective way to stop the spread of germs
explain: Correct: D — the whole passage explains how and why to wash hands well. A ('Germs are only spread in hospitals'): the passage never limits germs to hospitals. B ('Drying hands is more important than washing them'): drying is one step, not the main point. C ('Hand sanitizer works better than soap and water'): the passage says sanitizer is a backup, not better.

q: Nonmetals tend to be
options: poor conductors and brittle as solids
explain: Correct: A — nonmetals lack free electrons. B ('shiny and malleable'): that describes metals. C ('always gases'): some are solids like sulfur. D ('good conductors'): metals conduct well.

q:
Based on the passage about blood donation, why are iron-rich foods advised after donating?

Passage: Donated blood saves lives every day in surgeries, cancer treatment, and emergency care, and it cannot be manufactured. Donors must generally be healthy, meet age and weight requirements, and pass a brief health screening. The donation itself takes about ten minutes, during which roughly a pint of blood is collected; the body replaces the fluid within a day and the red cells within weeks. Donors are advised to eat iron-rich foods, drink extra fluids, and avoid heavy lifting with the donation arm afterward. Most healthy adults can donate whole blood every eight weeks.
options: To replace the donated plasma instantly
To help the body rebuild its red blood cells
explain: Correct: D — the body replaces red cells within weeks and iron supports that. A ('To make blood thicker permanently'): blood is not meant to thicken. B ('To prevent all future illness'): no such broad claim is made. C ('To replace the donated plasma instantly'): fluid, not iron, replaces volume quickly.

q: The nurse gave the patient ___ tablets with a glass of water.
explain: Correct: D — two is the number, which the sentence needs. A ('to'): to is a preposition showing direction. B ('too'): too means also or excessively. C ('tew'): tew is a misspelling.

q: The lungs, trachea, and bronchi make up the
explain: Correct: B — those organs exchange gases. A ('skeletal system'): skeletal supports. C ('cardiovascular system'): cardiovascular circulates blood. D ('nervous system'): nervous signals.

q:
According to the passage about fats, what do trans fats do?

Passage: Dietary fats have a bad reputation, but the body needs them to absorb certain vitamins, cushion organs, and build cell membranes. Unsaturated fats, found in olive oil, nuts, and fish, support heart health when they replace saturated fats. Saturated fats from butter, fatty meats, and full-fat dairy raise cholesterol when eaten in excess. Trans fats, once common in processed snacks, raise bad cholesterol and lower good cholesterol, and experts advise avoiding them. Reading labels for the type and amount of fat matters more than avoiding all fat.
options: Raise bad cholesterol and lower good cholesterol
explain: Correct: C — trans fats are said to raise bad and lower good cholesterol. A ('Build stronger bones'): bones are not mentioned. B ('Have no effect on health'): they are the most harmful type listed. D ('Lower both types of cholesterol'): they worsen the cholesterol balance.

q: Halogens are found in group
explain: Correct: A — group 17 holds the halogens. B ('2'): group 2 is alkaline earth. C ('18'): group 18 is noble gases. D ('1'): group 1 is alkali metals.

q: Choose the sentence with correct subject-verb agreement. (subject-verb agreement ('each'))
options: Each patient and visitor wearing a badge.
Each patient and visitor wear a badge.
Each patient and visitor wears a badge.
Each patient and visitor be wearing a badge.
explain: Correct: C — each makes the compound subject singular, so wears is correct. A ('Each patient and visitor wearing a badge.'): wearing is a participle, not a complete verb. B ('Each patient and visitor wear a badge.'): each keeps the subject singular despite and. D ('Each patient and visitor be wearing a badge.'): be wearing is not a correct present-tense form.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about sun protection?

Passage: Ultraviolet rays from the sun damage skin cells and raise the risk of skin cancer, yet much of that damage is preventable. Sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher, applied generously and reapplied every two hours, blocks most harmful rays. Protective clothing, wide-brimmed hats, and sunglasses add another layer of defense, and seeking shade between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. avoids the strongest sun. Tanning beds are not a safe alternative, since they also expose skin to cancer-causing ultraviolet radiation. Checking the skin regularly for new or changing moles helps catch problems early.
options: Tanning beds are a safe option
Sun damage is largely preventable with sunscreen, clothing, and shade
explain: Correct: C — the passage lists layered defenses against ultraviolet rays. A ('Tanning beds are a safe option'): tanning beds are explicitly unsafe. B ('Sunscreen alone guarantees no damage'): clothing and shade are also advised. D ('Moles never need checking'): regular skin checks are recommended.

q: In medical terminology, '-pnea' means
explain: Correct: D — -pnea relates to breathing, as in apnea. A ('pain'): is the meaning of -algia. B ('sleep'): uses the combining form somn-. C ('blood'): is the combining form hem-.

q: During which phase do sister chromatids separate?
explain: Correct: B — anaphase pulls chromatids apart. A ('Telophase'): telophase forms nuclei. C ('Metaphase'): metaphase aligns them. D ('Prophase'): prophase condenses chromosomes.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about nutrition labels?

Passage: Nutrition labels help shoppers compare foods and make informed choices. The serving size listed at the top is the key to the whole label: all the calories and nutrients shown are for one serving, not the entire package. Percent Daily Values tell how much a nutrient in a serving contributes to a day's diet, with five percent or less considered low and twenty percent or more considered high. Shoppers watching sodium, added sugars, or saturated fat can use these percentages to compare products quickly. Ingredients are listed from most to least by weight, so the first few ingredients make up most of the food.
options: Percent Daily Values are too confusing to use
Labels give shoppers the facts needed to compare foods wisely
explain: Correct: D — the passage explains how each label part helps shoppers. A ('Ingredients are listed alphabetically'): ingredients are listed by weight, most to least. B ('Serving sizes are always realistic'): serving sizes may differ from what people eat. C ('Percent Daily Values are too confusing to use'): the percentages are presented as a quick tool.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'profound'?
explain: Correct: C — profound means showing great depth of insight. A ('shallow'): is an antonym meaning not deep. B ('superficial'): means surface-level, the opposite of deep. D ('trivial'): means unimportant, not meaningful.

q: Which sentence uses the correct superlative form? (superlative form)
options: She is the more experienced nurse on the unit.
She is the most experienced nurse on the unit.
She is the most experienced nurse among the unit.
She is the experiencedest nurse on the unit.
explain: Correct: B — most experienced is the correct superlative. A ('She is the more experienced nurse on the unit.'): more is comparative, for two only. C ('She is the most experienced nurse among the unit.'): among is wrong with the superlative construction. D ('She is the experiencedest nurse on the unit.'): experiencedest is not a word.

q: The mesentery and serosa are associated with the
explain: Correct: C — they support abdominal organs. A ('lung pleura'): pleura wraps the lungs. B ('heart sac'): pericardium wraps the heart. D ('brain coverings'): meninges cover the brain.

q:
Based on the passage about stroke, why is noting when symptoms began important?

Passage: A stroke happens when blood flow to part of the brain is blocked or a brain vessel bursts, and fast treatment can prevent major disability. The FAST test helps bystanders recognize a stroke: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, and Time to call emergency services. Treatment works best within the first hours, so noting when symptoms began is critical. Risk factors include high blood pressure, smoking, diabetes, and atrial fibrillation. Calling for help immediately matters more than driving the person yourself, since paramedics can begin care on the way.
options: It replaces the need for FAST
It proves the stroke was minor
Treatment works best within the first hours
explain: Correct: D — treatment is time-sensitive, so onset time guides care. A ('It replaces the need for FAST'): FAST is still needed. B ('It proves the stroke was minor'): severity is not determined this way. C ('It determines the patient's age'): age is not the issue.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'terminate'?
explain: Correct: B — terminate means to bring to an end. A ('begin'): is an antonym meaning to start. C ('initiate'): means to start, the opposite of end. D ('commence'): means to begin formally, not to end.

q: In medical terminology, '-algia' means
explain: Correct: D — -algia means pain, as in neuralgia. A ('inflammation'): is the meaning of -itis. B ('tumor'): is the meaning of -oma. C ('discharge'): is the meaning of -rrhea.

q: Round 8.45 to the nearest tenth.
explain: Correct: A — The hundredths digit is 5, so round the tenths digit up: 8.5. B ('8'): rounded to the wrong place value. C ('8.4'): the digit was dropped without rounding up. D ('8.45'): no rounding was done at all.

q: Convert 9:05 PM to military time.
explain: Correct: D — Add 12 to a PM hour: 9 + 12 = 21, so 9:05 PM = 2105. A ('0905'): 12 was never added for the PM hour. B ('2005'): added 11 instead of 12. C ('0935'): the minutes were misread.

q: An acid donates
explain: Correct: C — acids release H+ in solution. A ('electrons'): electrons are not donated by acids. B ('neutrons'): neutrons stay in nuclei. D ('hydroxide ions (OH-)'): bases release OH-.

q: What do enzymes do in a reaction?
explain: Correct: B — enzymes speed reactions by lowering the energy barrier. A ('Change the products formed'): enzymes do not change the products. C ('Raise the activation energy'): that would slow reactions. D ('Get used up permanently'): enzymes are reusable.

q: Choose the sentence with parallel structure. (parallel structure (gerunds))
options: The nurse likes to chart, teaching, and mentor students.
The nurse likes charting, teaching, and mentoring students.
The nurse likes charting, teaching, and to mentor students.
The nurse likes charting, to teach, and mentoring students.
explain: Correct: B — all three items are gerunds, keeping the series parallel. A ('The nurse likes to chart, teaching, and mentor students.'): mixing infinitives and gerunds breaks parallelism. C ('The nurse likes charting, teaching, and to mentor students.'): to mentor breaks the gerund pattern. D ('The nurse likes charting, to teach, and mentoring students.'): to teach breaks the gerund pattern.

q: A price changes from $25 to $30. What is the percent increase?
explain: Correct: C — Change = 5; 5 / 25 = 0.20 = 20% increase. A ('20% decrease'): reported the dollar change as the percent. B ('5% increase'): got the direction of the change wrong. D ('17% increase'): divided by the new value instead of the original.

q: Hemophilia is an X-linked recessive trait. A carrier mother (XHXh) and normal father (XHY) can have
explain: Correct: C — sons get X from mother, so half of sons are affected. A ('no children with hemophilia'): affected sons are possible. B ('all sons with hemophilia'): only half of sons are affected. D ('only daughters with hemophilia'): daughters get a normal X from father.

q: In health care, the term 'lesion' means
explain: Correct: D — a lesion is a region of injured or diseased tissue. A ('scar'): is healed tissue. B ('swelling'): is edema, one possible sign. C ('bruise'): is a contusion, one kind of lesion.

q: Table salt (NaCl) is held together by
explain: Correct: A — sodium transfers an electron to chlorine. B ('hydrogen bonds'): hydrogen bonds are weaker attractions. C ('metallic bonds'): metallic bonds are in metals. D ('covalent bonds'): covalent bonds share electrons.

q: What number does the Roman numeral XC represent?
explain: Correct: B — 90 = 90, so XC = 90. A ('C'): uses the wrong additive combination. C ('XCC'): reverses part of the numeral. D ('LXXXX'): misreads the subtractive pair.

q: What is a gene?
options: A DNA segment coding for a protein
explain: Correct: A — genes are DNA instructions for proteins. B ('An energy molecule'): ATP is the energy molecule. C ('A whole chromosome'): chromosomes contain many genes. D ('A type of lipid'): lipids are fats.

q: Bones, cartilage, and ligaments make up the
explain: Correct: D — those tissues support and protect. A ('muscular system'): muscular moves the body. B ('nervous system'): nervous signals. C ('integumentary system'): integumentary is skin.

q: The medication will ___ the patient's heart rate.
explain: Correct: C — alter is the verb meaning to change. A ('halter'): halter is a strap, unrelated. B ('later'): later refers to time. D ('altar'): altar is a table used in worship.

q: Which of the following is a synonym for 'keen'?
explain: Correct: A — keen means intensely interested. B ('reluctant'): is an antonym meaning unwilling. C ('dull'): means blunt or uninterested, the opposite of eager. D ('apathetic'): means showing no interest, not keen.

q: Choose the sentence with correct subject-verb agreement. (subject-verb agreement ('the number'))
options: The number of admissions have increased.
A number of admissions has increased.
The number of admissions has increased.
The number of admissions have increase.
explain: Correct: C — the number is singular and takes has. A ('The number of admissions have increased.'): the subject is number, not admissions. B ('A number of admissions has increased.'): a number of is plural and needs have. D ('The number of admissions have increase.'): have is the wrong verb and increase needs the -d ending.

q: The brain and spinal cord make up the
explain: Correct: D — the CNS is brain plus spinal cord. A ('autonomic system'): autonomic is a peripheral division. B ('somatic system'): somatic is a peripheral division. C ('peripheral nervous system'): peripheral is nerves outside.

q:
According to the passage about MRSA, how does it mainly spread?

Passage: MRSA is a type of staph bacteria resistant to many common antibiotics, making its infections harder to treat. It often appears as a painful, swollen, pus-filled skin bump that can be mistaken for a spider bite. MRSA spreads through skin-to-skin contact and shared items like towels and razors, thriving in gyms, locker rooms, and health care settings. Prevention centers on handwashing, keeping cuts covered, and not sharing personal items. Suspected MRSA should be evaluated promptly rather than squeezed, since improper handling can spread the infection.
options: Through the air over long distances
Through skin-to-skin contact and shared items
explain: Correct: D — contact and shared items are the stated routes. A ('Through the air over long distances'): airborne spread is not stated. B ('Through contaminated drinking water'): water is not mentioned. C ('Through insect bites'): it is mistaken for bites, not caused by them.

q: What is the monomer of nucleic acids?
explain: Correct: C — nucleotides chain into DNA and RNA. A ('Glycerol'): glycerol is part of lipids. B ('Glucose'): glucose builds carbohydrates. D ('Amino acid'): amino acids build proteins.

q:
What is the main idea of the passage about protein?

Passage: Protein is made of building blocks called amino acids, and the body uses them to build and repair muscle, skin, enzymes, and hormones. Because the body does not store protein the way it stores fat, a steady supply from food is needed each day. Complete proteins, which contain all essential amino acids, come from animal foods as well as soy and quinoa. Incomplete proteins from beans, grains, and nuts can be combined across the day to meet needs. Most people eating a varied diet get enough protein without supplements.
options: Protein repairs the body, needs daily intake, and comes from varied foods
explain: Correct: C — the passage covers function, daily need, and sources. A ('Only meat provides complete protein'): soy and quinoa are complete plant proteins. B ('Protein is stored like fat'): the body does not store protein. D ('Supplements are required for everyone'): most varied diets provide enough.

q:
Based on the passage about pneumonia, why would a clinician ask whether the illness is bacterial or viral?

Passage: Pneumonia is an infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid or pus. Symptoms include cough with phlegm, fever, chills, and difficulty breathing. It can be caused by bacteria, viruses, or fungi, and treatment depends on the cause: bacterial pneumonia needs antibiotics, while viral cases need rest and supportive care. Older adults, young children, and people with weakened immunity face the highest risk of complications. Vaccines against pneumococcal bacteria and the flu lower the risk of the most common forms.
options: Because antibiotics only help bacterial pneumonia
Because the question is purely for records
Because all cases get the same treatment
